text.overview: The Mortar Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle mounting three Class 8 Mech Mortars on the standard carrier chassis. Developed by the Quikscell Company in 3083, the design is a Dark Age evolution of the weapons carrier concept, providing indirect fire capability through ballistic mortar bombardment rather than guided missiles. The fuel cell engine and heavy ferro-fibrous armor distinguish it from earlier carrier designs.
text.capabilities:
The Mortar Carrier mounts three forward-firing Class 8 Mech Mortars, providing indirect fire capability through ballistic bombardment. A 180-rated fuel cell engine replaces the traditional internal combustion powerplant, maintaining fifty-four kilometer per hour speed with cleaner operation. Aldis Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor provides eighty-nine points of protection, nearly double the standard carrier family's coverage.

A Communicator system and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting provide fire direction capability. The mortar system fires in a high ballistic arc, allowing engagement of targets behind terrain features and buildings. The substantially improved armor protection and fuel cell engine represent a generational leap over earlier carrier designs, though at increased production cost.
text.deployment: Quikscell plants on Richvale, Kalidasa, and Layover produce the Mortar Carrier alongside Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium on Maxwell. The design entered service in 3083, filling an indirect fire role in Dark Age-era combined-arms formations.
text.battleHistory:
The Mortar Carrier was developed by Quikscell in 3083 during the early Dark Age, applying the weapons carrier concept to Mech Mortar technology. The design replaced the SRM Carrier's missile launchers with three Class 8 Mech Mortars on the same basic chassis, though the fuel cell engine and heavy ferro-fibrous armor represent significant departures from earlier carrier designs.

Production was established at Quikscell plants on Richvale, Kalidasa, and Layover, supplemented by Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium on Maxwell. The mortar system's indirect fire capability and area-effect munitions filled a tactical gap between direct-fire carriers and dedicated artillery platforms.

text.overview: The MRM Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle mounting three MRM-30 launchers on the standard carrier chassis. Developed by the Quikscell Company as a variant of the SRM/LRM Carrier family, the MRM Carrier emerged during the FedCom Civil War era to exploit medium-range missile technology. A C3 slave unit enables networked targeting to compensate for the MRM system's inherent inaccuracy at extended range.
text.capabilities:
The MRM Carrier mounts three MRM-30 launchers as its primary armament, supplemented by a C3 slave unit for networked targeting data. An InterComBust 180 internal combustion engine maintains the standard fifty-four kilometer per hour top speed. Lexington Ltd. High Grade ferro-fibrous armor provides fifty-three points of protection, improved over the standard carrier's Simple Armor Plate.

A Communicator system with C3 link and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting enable coordination with C3 master units. Each MRM-30 launcher carries only eight rounds, giving the vehicle limited endurance before requiring resupply. The MRM system's inherent scatter pattern makes it most effective against clustered targets or in area-denial roles.
text.deployment: Quikscell produced the MRM Carrier at its Oliver facility beginning around 3063. The design found modest adoption across the Inner Sphere, often paired with ECM-equipped units to protect the slow-moving carrier from electronic countermeasures during engagements.
text.battleHistory:
The MRM Carrier was introduced by Quikscell as a variant during the FedCom Civil War era, mounting three MRM-30 launchers with a C3 slave unit on the standard carrier chassis. TRO:3058 Upgrade describes it as 'almost an entirely new design,' noting that it is often paired with ECM-equipped units as it is too slow to keep up in swift advances. Each launcher carries only eight rounds, requiring frequent resupply.

Quikscell produced the MRM Carrier at its Oliver facility for distribution across the Inner Sphere. The design found modest popularity as a middle-ground between the long-range LRM Carrier and the close-range SRM Carrier, though limited ammunition capacity remained a persistent complaint.

text.deployment: The standard Musketeer deploys throughout the AFFS in combined-arms battalions and independent screening formations. Its hover chassis provides the cross-terrain flexibility to keep pace with faster strike elements while the RAC/5 delivers sustained fire capable of stripping armor from enemy vehicles and suppressing BattleMechs. AFFS militia units along the Draconis Combine and Capellan borders received early priority deliveries, and the design saw active combat during the FedCom Civil War within its first years of service. It is most effective in open or semi-open terrain where the hover chassis can exploit its speed advantage.

The (3080 Upgrade) incorporates system refinements drawn from Civil War and Jihad combat experience, improving reliability and reducing maintenance demands without substantially altering the vehicle's role or armament philosophy. It is primarily deployed with AFFS formations that accumulated field experience with the base design and requested updated equipment as part of post-Jihad reconstitution. The variant represents the mature production form of the Musketeer line and extended the design's service life through the Dark Age period.

The (Armor) variant replaces the standard model's RAC/5 with a lighter RAC/2 system and divides the recovered tonnage between additional ferro-fibrous armor protection and expanded ammunition storage. The extended range and improved ammunition efficiency of the RAC/2 make this configuration well-suited for extended operations away from established supply lines. Unit commanders who prioritize vehicle survivability and operational endurance over burst-fire output generally favor this variant, and it is frequently assigned to missions where resupply cannot be guaranteed.

production.manufacturer: New Earth Trading Company|Jalastar Aerospace|Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium

components.armor: New Earth Trading Company ArcShield Maxi II

text.deployment: The standard Myrmidon found its primary market among Lyran Alliance commands reinforcing the Clan border, and among independent and mercenary forces operating throughout the Chaos March. Jalastar's licensed production on Panpour supplied AFFS requirements through the Civil War and Jihad eras. Following the destruction of NETC's New Earth facility, Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium resumed manufacture on Maxwell under license from approximately 3088, sustaining supply through the Republic period and into the ilClan era under Capellan administration of the Maxwell system.

The Anti-Infantry variant emerged from Jalastar Aerospace's investigation of a pirate-modified Myrmidon encountered on Kolovraty during the Jihad. After securing a production license from NETC, Jalastar reconfigured the design to mount an extended-range large laser in the main turret and six light machine guns across paired sponson turrets, replacing the PPC to avoid undercutting Jalastar's own Manticore sales. The revised loadout delivers exceptional effectiveness against unarmored infantry at close range but sacrifices the long-range striking power of the original design.

Initial AFFS adoption was slow, as procurement officers preferred direct-fire platforms. The variant found wider acceptance with Republic Armed Forces units patrolling the Confederation border, and mercenary commands attracted by the low acquisition cost became consistent buyers. Jalastar reinvested profits from Anti-Infantry production back into the Manticore line, using the revenue to reduce Manticore prices to AFFS for the following decade.

This experimental pirate modification, first documented during raids attributed to the mercenary band Breed's Brawlers in 3075, swaps the standard particle projection cannon for a snub-nose PPC and mounts twin sponson machine gun arrays for close-range anti-infantry work. Light ferro-fibrous armor provides marginally improved protection at the cost of manufacturing complexity, an unusual investment for a field refit. The vehicle was implicated in deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure on Kolovraty, drawing substantial bounties from both the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces and ComStar. The configuration has never been formally replicated and remains a singular example of pirate-modified Myrmidon technology.

text.overview: The Nacon Armored Scout was developed by Trellshire Heavy Industries on Sudeten in anticipation of Clan Jade Falcon's eventual desant into the Republic of the Sphere. Introduced in 3096, the design addresses a practical gap in Jade Falcon combined-arms doctrine, providing a fast and expendable reconnaissance platform capable of keeping pace with OmniMechs without consuming the logistical resources required to field additional BattleMechs. Named for a Mayan war god, the designation strikes most Inner Sphere observers as somewhat grandiose for an armored scout car, and even Clan warriors tend to view the official name as a stretch given the vehicle's limited offensive profile. Despite this skepticism, the Nacon reliably fulfills its intended role, delivering performance that has repeatedly exceeded the modest expectations accompanying its introduction to Jade Falcon touman formations.
text.capabilities:
The Nacon is built around speed and resilience for its weight class. The Starfire 180 XL fusion engine drives the wheeled chassis to a maximum speed of 162 kilometers per hour, allowing it to outpace most opposition and disengage from engagements it cannot win. A System 4 ATM-6 launcher forms the primary armament, offering tactical flexibility through standard, extended-range, or high-explosive ammunition loads. This adaptability makes the Nacon useful against a range of target types, from armored vehicles to dispersed infantry concentrations. Two Series 34NC Light Machine Guns supplement the ATM launcher, providing effective close-in defense against conventional infantry attempting to close with the vehicle.

The Nacon carries substantially more armor than most vehicles in its weight class, with Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous protection allowing it to absorb punishment that would disable lighter scouts. This survivability is critical to its bait-and-switch role, where the vehicle must attract fire and then withdraw in reasonable condition. The design's most significant weakness lies in its rear armor plating, which is noticeably thin. When the Nacon performs its intended function of drawing opponents into the weapons envelope of accompanying BattleMechs, it exposes this vulnerable aspect to any enemy that declines to pursue. Commanders consistently rate the Nacon highest in infantry screening and bait-and-switch operations, and lowest when required to hold a position without heavier fire support nearby.
text.deployment: The Nacon Armored Scout remains largely in service with Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Sea Fox, though a meaningful number have entered mercenary hands through Diamond Shark trade networks. Within Jade Falcon formations, the vehicle operates in combined-arms elements alongside OmniMechs, handling forward screening, route reconnaissance, and infantry suppression ahead of advancing BattleMech stars. Sea Fox operators deploy the Nacon in comparable roles, frequently as pickets for garrison detachments or advance security for trade convoys. Mercenary operators typically assign the design to scouting and screening duties where its speed and armor resilience offset the relatively limited range of its ATM launcher.
text.battleHistory:
Trellshire Heavy Industries completed the Nacon's development on Sudeten in 3096, responding to Jade Falcon operational planning that anticipated large-scale conventional forces would be essential to support the Clan's push into the Republic of the Sphere. The design entered Jade Falcon service with little ceremony, viewed by many warriors as a concession to practical necessity rather than an expression of Clan combat doctrine.

The Nacon saw its first significant combat during the Falcons' desant, deploying across Republic Prefectures VIII and IX. On Chaffee, armored scout elements operated primarily against planetary militia formations that lacked the weapons to threaten the swift vehicle, validating the design's value in asymmetric engagements. The battle for Skye in mid-3134 proved more demanding. Nacon elements conducted continuous reconnaissance and screening operations at the vanguard of Jade Falcon advances, identifying ambush positions and drawing out Republic defenders ahead of the main force. The fighting demonstrated that the vehicle's survivability margins were genuinely sufficient for contested-space reconnaissance rather than merely low-threat scouting.

At Weston Heights, Nacons were committed in force to reconnaissance sweeps attempting to locate Republic troop concentrations. Units that successfully baited heavier Republic elements found them pounced upon by Jade Falcon BattleMechs before reinforcements could arrive. The majority of scout cars deployed to these operations were lost, but the intelligence they generated was considered operationally decisive by Falcon commanders.

By 3135, the Nacon had also begun attracting outside interest. A Third Falcon Swoop Cluster operation on Zoetermeer pitted a Binary of light BattleMechs and Nacons against Wolf garrison forces from the Twentieth Wolf Regulars. The Wolf commanders focused fire on the Falcon OmniMechs, treating the scout vehicles as secondary targets. The Nacon drivers exploited this misstep, pressing Wolf infantry and light armor while the Falcon BattleMechs maneuvered. The Falcons secured their objectives, and the engagement drew attention from Clan Sea Fox, who subsequently acquired a considerable number of Nacons for resale through mercenary networks.

text.capabilities:
The Narukami's primary armament consists of a Grizzard Model 200 Gauss Rifle paired with two Lord's Light Particle Projection Cannons, a combination designed to engage targets well beyond the effective range of most opposing armor. Two Chosatsugai no Kunai Anti-Missile Systems provide reliable point defense, protecting the crew and ammunition stores from incoming missile fire. The New Samarkand Teppeki Hardened armor, installed with integral CASE to contain potential ammunition explosions, provides substantial protection against weapons fire, with the hardened construction offering additional resistance that standard armor cannot match. A GM 270 XL fusion engine gives the 90-ton vehicle adequate ground speed for defensive operations and siege work, though the design's critics have noted it leaves the Narukami slower than many opponents would prefer.

The design carries notable trade-offs. The XL engine reduces the vehicle's mass but increases vulnerability to internal destruction if the engine bays are penetrated. The Gauss rifle's reliance on discrete ammunition rounds creates logistical demands that must be planned for in extended campaigns. The PPC pair generates heat that, while manageable for a combat vehicle, stresses cooling systems during sustained engagements. These factors combine to make the Narukami a capable but demanding platform that rewards careful crew training and robust supply chain management.
text.deployment: The NK-1C serves as a standard fire support unit across frontline and second-line DCMS armor regiments. Attrition over decades of conflict has concentrated surviving examples in the New Samarkand Regulars and the Legions of Vega, where proximity to the manufacturing facilities facilitates resupply and maintenance. The variant is deployed most effectively in defensive lines and contested corridor operations, where its long-range weapons suite can be used to full advantage. Field commanders favor the NK-1C for siege operations and prepared defensive positions, where its modest ground speed is a lesser concern.

text.capabilities:
The BC3 chassis mounts paired Grizzard Gauss rifles in place of the single rifle of the base model, offering substantially greater firepower at long range. Two Lord's Light Particle Projection Cannons are retained, and the advanced C3 support system allows the variant to coordinate targeting data across a fire network, making each shot more precise than the individual crew could achieve alone. The Omicron IX targeting suite is supplemented with C3 slave equipment, and the vehicle's defensive suite and armor remain identical to the NK-1C.

The trade-offs are significant. The second Gauss rifle consumes ammunition at twice the rate of the base model, placing considerable strain on logistics trains during extended operations. The C3 system is also dependent on a functional command network, meaning the variant loses much of its tactical advantage when operating independently or when its supporting command units are destroyed. The vehicle performs best when supported by a coherent combined-arms force with reliable communications, and its value diminishes sharply when that network is disrupted.
text.deployment: The NK-BC3 is deployed exclusively in units equipped with C3 fire control networks, where it functions as a frontline sniper coordinating fire with lighter, faster elements. The variant's paired Gauss rifle configuration delivers greater raw firepower than the base model, but the associated ammunition requirements have repeatedly complicated extended operations far from supply depots. The DCMS has concentrated BC3 examples in units operating along the Federated Suns border, where command networks can make full use of the variant's targeting coordination capabilities.

The standard Neptune entered service with the AFFS in 2950, deployed primarily to worlds along the Draconis and Capellan Marches with significant ocean coverage and established underwater command infrastructure. Early deployments concentrated on Draconis March frontier worlds, where the threat of Combine naval or amphibious incursion was most acute. The Neptune performed its designed role with competence, patrolling assigned sectors and escorting underwater command facilities. Its limited torpedo reloads required coordinating Neptune deployments in pairs or small groups to maintain continuous coverage without gaps in patrol cycles.

text.capabilities:
The Neptune displaces one hundred tons and is driven by a Doorman 270 Naval HyPerOx propulsion system capable of pushing the vessel to a maximum speed of 54 kilometers per hour whether submerged or running on the surface. The engine can operate in open-cycle diesel mode on the surface or switch to hydrogen peroxide combustion for deep-water operation, providing tactical flexibility across varying depth requirements. A conventional double-hull construction separates the pressure hull from the outer hull, providing structural redundancy and a rated dive depth exceeding one kilometer. Six crew members occupy the interior, and their working conditions are especially cramped given the volume consumed by machinery and ammunition storage.

The primary offensive system is the Sea Devastator 20-rack torpedo battery, a marinized version of long-range missile technology with excellent range and firepower against surface and subsurface targets. Two Sea Harvester six-rack torpedo launchers provide close-range punch, ensuring the Neptune can engage across the tactical envelope. A Sutel XII large laser serves as a secondary weapon for surface engagements and situations where torpedo expenditure must be conserved. The Neptune's chief tactical weakness is limited torpedo reloads, which constrains its ability to sustain prolonged combat operations without resupply support.
text.deployment: Introduced by Galtor Naval Yards in 3024, the Hunter-Killer is a purpose-built anti-submarine warfare variant designed to locate and destroy opposing submarine forces rather than defend fixed underwater installations. Its refined sensor package and weapons configuration optimize performance in direct submarine-versus-submarine engagements, filling a tactical niche that the standard Neptune could only partially address. The variant saw its first operational deployments during the Fourth Succession War, defending key Federated Suns coastal systems against Combine submarine interdiction. Following the formation of the Federated Commonwealth, GNY supplied the Hunter-Killer to both AFFS and LAAF commands with active undersea interdiction requirements, with production maintained at both the Exeter and Galtor facilities.

The LRT configuration replaces the Sutel XII large laser with an additional Sea Devastator 20-rack torpedo installation and expanded ammunition capacity. Where the standard Neptune relies on the laser as a secondary weapon, the LRT variant doubles down on long-range torpedo saturation. Commands deploying Neptunes as convoy escorts or operating against well-defended deep targets favored this arrangement, as the added torpedo capacity allowed more sustained engagements before the submarine required resupply. The LRT variant is common in areas where torpedo logistics were reliable enough to support its greater consumption rate, particularly along heavily defended frontier worlds.

The original Nightshade served as the SLDF's primary airborne electronic warfare asset, deployed in support of combined-arms formations. Small teams of Nightshades operated ahead of advancing lances and companies, disrupting enemy communications before withdrawing behind friendly lines. The design was most effective when paired with heavier units that could exploit the confusion the Guardian ECM created. The light armor and single medium laser meant pilots had no margin for error if caught in direct engagement, and operational doctrine emphasized rapid repositioning over sustained presence in contested airspace.

The (Armor) field refit appeared during the Early Succession Wars as technicians worked to extend the operational life of surviving Nightshades. An XL fusion engine swap freed sufficient tonnage to mount a large pulse laser and add ferro-fibrous armor plating, directly addressing the original design's fragility. The conversion was performed at various facilities by units that retained both operational Nightshades and the technical skill to modify them. The rarity of surviving airframes and the difficulty of sourcing XL fusion engine components limited this refit to isolated examples scattered among the militias of the Succession States. No centralized production record exists.

Developed as a companion to the (Light PPC) model and entering production in 3070, the (LAC) variant replaced the particle cannon with a light autocannon and added target acquisition gear to support indirect fire missions. The combination proved effective when coordinating with artillery batteries, allowing the VTOL to provide rapid targeting solutions while its speed enabled it to avoid counterbattery fire. Like the (Light PPC) version, production was centered at Terra and distribution was concentrated in Word of Blake Protectorate formations. Unlike its C³i-equipped sibling, the simpler electronics made this variant more broadly useful, and production continued at Terra under the Republic of the Sphere through the Dark Age period.

Produced exclusively at Terra by MSDC under Word of Blake sponsorship, the (Light PPC) variant was distributed throughout Protectorate Militia divisions and served as the Blake forces' standard airborne ECM and reconnaissance platform. Its C³i integration made it most effective coordinating with other Blakist networked units, and Blake doctrine paired small groups of Nightshades with larger combined-arms formations rather than deploying them independently. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere discontinued the variant due to the C³i requirement. Surviving examples appeared in mercenary service, typically drawn from former Protectorate militia inventories.

The Royal variant was issued to selected SLDF units as a dedicated electronic warfare platform, incorporating enhanced Star League electronics beyond the standard production specification. Deployment was concentrated in SLDF formations with the maintenance infrastructure required to support the advanced components. The Royal's production window was short, and the loss of Yelm's facilities during the Amaris Crisis meant surviving examples became irreplaceable within a generation of the Exodus. The variant's advanced systems made it a priority target for capture or salvage, and few are believed to have survived the Succession Wars in operable condition.

The standard Nisos configuration mounts a Ceres Arms Crusher plasma rifle and a Harpoon-6 SRM launcher in a single turret, providing a balanced mix of energy suppression and missile striking power. This loadout makes the base variant well-suited for its intended role as an interdictor, capable of engaging both armored vehicles and infantry in the open. Two tons of plasma rifle ammunition and one ton of SRM reloads ensure adequate endurance for extended reconnaissance patrols. The Nisos serves primarily with CCAF scout and cavalry formations, where its speed allows it to screen advancing forces or pursue retreating enemies across varied terrain.

Introduced in 3123, the Support variant replaces the standard Nisos armament with a pair of ER medium lasers and a single Extended LRM 10 with eighteen rounds of ammunition. This configuration shifts the vehicle from a close-range interdictor to a fire-support platform capable of engaging targets at extended ranges. The ER medium lasers provide energy-based firepower that eliminates ammunition dependency for the primary weapons, while the Extended LRM gives the Support variant the ability to contribute indirect fire from well behind the front line. The trade-off is a significant reduction in short-range combat effectiveness, making the Support variant more reliant on other units for close defense.

text.overview: The Nuberu Anti-Aircraft Tank was one of the final joint projects between Clan Snow Raven and the Outworlds Alliance prior to the formation of the Raven Alliance. Entering production in 3083 at the United Outworlders Corporation facility on Mitchella, the Nuberu was designed to address the critical shortage of air defense assets plaguing the Alliance's ground forces after the Jihad. With pirate activity surging across the expanded Raven Alliance territories and the Aerospace Arm stretched too thin to provide adequate coverage, Snow Raven engineers partnered with their native Outworlder counterparts to create an improved anti-aircraft platform based on the proven Partisan concept. The collaboration produced a vehicle that costs less than two-thirds of a comparable Partisan Air Defense Tank.
text.capabilities:
The Nuberu's most distinctive feature is its innovative twin-turret design, splitting four Clan-grade Type OVR-X LB 5-X autocannons between two independent weapon mounts. This arrangement ensures that if one turret is disabled, the vehicle retains half its firepower and can continue engaging targets. The TRTTS Mark V AirTracker targeting system provides very accurate fire against airborne targets, though it is somewhat inaccurate against ground-based threats and the targeting computer often has problems attempting to track every missile.

Nine and a half tons of Clan laser-reflective armor significantly increase the vehicle's resistance to strafing attacks from energy weapon-armed aerospace fighters, the most deadly threat in the typical operating environment. A Jones ElectroCell 180 fuel cell engine provides a modest 54 km/h top speed, prioritizing affordability and simplicity over the fusion powerplants of more expensive designs. Ammunition endurance is limited, with only two tons of cluster rounds for the four autocannons, but as a defensive vehicle operating close to friendly supply lines, this is not considered a significant liability. The fuel cell engine and Clan manufacturing techniques keep production costs well below fusion-powered equivalents, enabling the Raven Alliance to field them in large numbers.
text.deployment: Every Raven Alliance garrison fields at least two platoons of Nuberus, with many possessing a full company. The vehicle's affordable production cost has allowed rapid fielding across the Alliance's dispersed territories, freeing aerospace fighters and BattleMechs from static defensive assignments. Deployment concentrations are heaviest on worlds with significant industrial or military infrastructure.
text.battleHistory:
The post-Jihad expansion of the Raven Alliance brought security challenges that no amount of Clan martial tradition could resolve through BattleMech deployments alone. With Clan Snow Raven's forces concentrated in their newly captured Draconis Combine holdings and suffering heavy touman losses, many Raven enclaves across the former Outworlds Alliance had been stripped of troops. The Jihad had been kinder to the Alliance than to many other realms, but the erosion of central authority led to a marked increase in pirate bands preying on the scattered, poorly defended worlds. With attacks occurring almost daily, the Alliance Aerospace Arm could no longer serve as the first line of defense, leaving ground forces critically exposed to air attack.

The answer, in the eyes of Snow Raven engineers, was obvious: the Inner Sphere had solved this problem centuries ago with the Partisan Heavy Tank and its descendants. The Raven Alliance needed a vehicle that could provide the same mobile air defense coverage, freeing aerospace fighters and BattleMechs from static defensive assignments. The Ravens initially suggested licensing the Partisan directly from Kallon Industries in the Federated Suns. Relations with House Davion remained strained from recent hostilities, however, and it was believed unlikely that the Alliance could secure the design. The attempt to obtain the Partisan through diplomatic channels failed, but it confirmed the design's reputation as the benchmark for dedicated anti-aircraft vehicles.

Instead, Snow Raven engineers partnered with their Outworlder counterparts at the United Outworlders Corporation on Mitchella. The collaboration divided responsibilities along each partner's strengths: the Ravens supplied engineering expertise, electronics, weapons, and armor technology, while the Outworlders provided manufacturing capacity, chassis production, and the fuel cell engine. The result was the Nuberu, named for the Asturian cloud spirit, a vehicle that used Clan technology to improve upon the Partisan concept while costing less than two-thirds of a comparable Partisan Air Defense Tank.

The Nuberu's innovative twin-turret design set it apart from every other vehicle in the Partisan lineage. By splitting its four Clan-grade LB 5-X autocannons between two independent mounts, the vehicle could continue fighting with half its firepower even after losing a turret. This redundancy was particularly valued by garrison commanders who could not count on rapid reinforcement. Clan laser-reflective armor provided exceptional protection against the energy weapons typical of pirate and bandit aerospace fighters, the most common airborne threat in Raven Alliance space.

Only in production since 3083, the Nuberu has proliferated rapidly across the Alliance. Every Raven garrison carries at least two platoons, with many possessing a full company or more. Deployments to defend significant installations have allowed far more fighters and BattleMechs to be released from static defensive duties. Most Raven enclaves maintain two Stars of the tank, often split into sub-units of two or more Points for distributed coverage. An entire Cluster of Nuberus has been observed on Alpheratz, defending the construction site of the Raven Alliance's new capital enclave.

The Numantia support variant, mounting Streak SRM 6s and LRM 15 launchers in place of the standard autocannons, addressed the base model's lack of secondary weapons. Deployed at a rate of one to two per platoon, the Numantia provides anti-infantry capability and indirect fire support that complements the standard model's dedicated anti-aircraft role.

The Nuberu is a significant milestone in the Partisan legacy. For nearly three centuries, the Partisan family had been exclusively an Inner Sphere design, produced by Kallon Industries for the armies of the Successor States. The Nuberu broke that monopoly, demonstrating that the mobile air defense doctrine the Partisan had pioneered was valuable enough to inspire independent development on the Periphery. Together with the Combine's Nike Air Defense Platform, the Nuberu confirmed that the Partisan's greatest contribution was not any single vehicle but the concept of dedicated, mobile, ground-based air defense itself.

text.overview:
The Odin Scout Tank is a lightweight Clan reconnaissance vehicle introduced in 2844. Weighing only twenty tons, the wheeled tank was designed from the outset as a dedicated intelligence-gathering platform rather than a combat vehicle. Its sophisticated sensor suite and impressive top speed made it one of the premier scouting assets available to any Clan's touman. Production spread across nearly every Clan's homeworld industrial base, evidence of the design's universal appeal and straightforward manufacturing requirements.

Despite the Clans' well-documented disdain for conventional vehicles, the Odin carved out a lasting niche by excelling in a role that most warriors considered beneath them. Few other vehicles achieved such widespread adoption among so many different Clans, and the design's longevity across centuries of service speaks to its fundamental soundness as a reconnaissance platform.
text.deployment: The base Odin serves as the standard reconnaissance variant across Clan military forces. Produced at numerous facilities throughout the Kerensky Cluster and later at Inner Sphere factories, it remains one of the most widely distributed scout vehicles in any Clan touman. Contrary to Clan tradition, the two-person crew often trains together and serves as a team throughout their military career, a strategy required by the high level of coordination needed to effectively operate the vehicle's complex sensor systems while maneuvering at high speed.

text.deployment:
The Spotter variant stands as a significant reimagining of the Odin's role, shifting the vehicle from active reconnaissance to dedicated artillery support and target designation. Developed for the Kungsarme in 3071, this variant replaces the fusion engine with a fuel cell powerplant while maintaining the original top speed. The freed weight accommodates an ECM suite, target acquisition gear, and a Narc missile beacon, transforming the Odin into a potent force multiplier for indirect fire assets.

All original weaponry was stripped in favor of a pair of anti-personnel Gauss rifles, providing minimal self-defense capability. The Spotter's reliance on friendly fire support made it unappealing to Clan warriors, and no Clans expressed interest in the design despite its Inner Sphere origins at Joint Equipment Systems on Alshain.

Though originally built in Capellan space, the Ontos was highly favored by House Marik after the League captured Shiro III during the Succession Wars. After the annexation of Nanking by the Federated Commonwealth, the vehicle formed the backbone of many Free Worlds League heavy tank regiments. The larger-than-average vehicle formations favored by the Marik military gave the heavy tanks plenty of support to offset their short range.

production.targeting: GuideRite with Laser Coordination Link and Artemis FCS

text.deployment: Produced exclusively at Grumman's Shiro III facility, the upgraded Ontos entered service during the Clan Invasion era. Deployed with Marik, Capellan, Steiner, and Davion units, it also found its way to mercenary commands and the Touman of Clan Nova Cat. Despite improvements, the older variants remained common alongside the upgrade across multiple factions.

Produced at Grumman's facilities on Shiro III and a new plant on Trellisane within the Wolf Empire, the Chemical Laser variant represents the latest evolution of the Ontos. Forces expecting the traditional medium laser battery face a significant surprise from both the extended range and hitting power of the chemical laser armament.

The fusion-powered Ontos saw limited initial production, as the rarity and expense of fusion engines during the Succession Wars restricted distribution. Individual units and well-supplied garrison commands sometimes attempted the conversion, with mixed results. Kallon's Nanking facility began dedicated production of the Fusion variant after upgrading its lines in 3059, expanding availability significantly.

Grumman initially restricted sales of the Light Gauss variant to the Capellan Confederation and the Free Worlds League. Commercial interest and the outbreak of war loosened these restrictions over time. The variant filled an armored sniper role, harassing and softening enemy formations before engagement, a significant departure from the original Ontos doctrine.

The LRM variant was a common field modification throughout the Succession Wars, replacing the energy weapon array with a more conventional missile loadout. Crews who preferred engaging at range or operating in combined-arms formations often favored this conversion, which traded the Ontos's signature sustained-fire capability for greater striking power at distance.

Developed during the Jihad, the MML variant combined long-range and short-range missile capabilities alongside residual Gauss armament in a versatile package. Both factory-produced models from Grumman's Shiro III facility and field refit conversions of existing Light Gauss Ontos tanks saw deployment across multiple factions during the chaotic fighting of that era and beyond.

The sealed Ontos was designed for amphibious and hostile-environment operations during the Jihad. It saw service in littoral combat zones and on worlds where atmospheric conditions required environmental protection. Grumman produced the variant at Shiro III, while field conversion kits allowed existing Ontos tanks to be sealed for specific deployments.

The Ontos HEAT is deployed in small numbers wherever local environmental conditions are a primary concern. Notable postings include worlds heavily damaged during the Jihad, such as Hesperus II and Tharkad. Quikscell has restricted most sales to the Lyran Commonwealth, though the Capellan Confederation and Free Worlds League have also acquired limited numbers.

Configuration A replaces the Prime's close-range armament with an ER PPC and four AP Gauss Rifles sharing a single ton of ammunition, supported by five additional heat sinks. This transforms the Onuris into a long-range sniper platform capable of engaging targets well outside return fire range. The AP Gauss Rifles provide effective point defense against infantry and battle armor that might threaten the VTOL during low-altitude operations.

Configuration B mounts twin LRM-20 launchers with four tons of ammunition, converting the Onuris into a dedicated missile platform. The sustained indirect fire capability makes this configuration valuable for suppressing fixed positions and softening defensive lines before ground forces advance. Standard Onuris Stars typically include a single Point of B variants to provide long-range fire support for the closer-ranged Prime and A configurations.

Configuration C carries an LB 20-X autocannon with two tons of ammunition, one slug and one cluster. This loadout delivers devastating short-range firepower, with cluster rounds proving particularly effective against light vehicles, conventional infantry, and other VTOLs. The configuration has earned a reputation among Rasalhague Dominion opponents for its ability to rapidly immobilize enemy vehicles with concentrated cluster fire before disengaging at speed.

Configuration D emphasizes energy weapons, mounting two Improved Heavy Medium Lasers and five Medium Chemical Lasers with three tons of chemical laser ammunition. Four additional heat sinks manage the increased thermal load. This variant was derived from the Red Kite fighter design produced in the Free Worlds League, and its laser-heavy loadout reduces dependence on ammunition resupply. The combination of accurate improved lasers and sustained chemical laser fire provides consistent damage output across extended engagements.

Configuration E balances a Large Pulse Laser with an ATM 9 launcher carrying one ton each of Standard, Extended Range, and High Explosive ammunition. This loadout offers the widest engagement envelope of any Onuris configuration, from extended-range ATM shots to close-range pulse laser strikes. Two Points of E variants distinguished themselves during Clan Wolf operations on Shiloh, using jet boosters to overtake Republic scouts before destroying them with combined pulse laser and ATM fire.

The Prime serves as the standard strike configuration, carrying a plasma cannon and four SRM-6 launchers with two tons of plasma and three tons of SRM ammunition. Deployed in pairs as part of standard Onuris Stars, the Prime's plasma cannon generates dangerous heat buildup in enemy units, setting them up for the devastating SRM barrage that follows. This configuration formed the backbone of Task Force Navarre's initial Onuris deployments against the Capellan Home Guard.

The standard Oro sees service across numerous Clan toumans in garrison and second-line roles. Its combination of long-range pulse laser fire and devastating close-range autocannon capability makes it effective in both defensive positions and mobile engagements. Vehicle Stars frequently pair Oros with lighter scout vehicles, using the heavy tank's firepower to anchor defensive screens. The design's dual-purpose ammunition capability allows commanders to tailor their loadout to anticipated threats, selecting slug rounds for armored targets or cluster munitions for anti-air duties.

Introduced in 3073, the HAG variant replaces the LB-20X autocannon and extended-range medium laser with a single Type 0 Class 30 hyper-assault Gauss rifle and sixteen rounds of ammunition. Armor protection is doubled from the baseline model, significantly improving survivability. The Kolibri Delta large pulse laser is retained as a secondary weapon. Originally discovered in Snow Raven service near the Outworlds Alliance border, this variant may have been designed to train Raven pilots to counter the emerging hyper-assault Gauss threat, or it may reflect a broader shift in Raven design priorities. Alliance Defenders Limited on Alpheratz produces this variant under Raven Alliance authority.

The standard fusion-powered Packrat serves as the baseline reconnaissance and deep patrol vehicle across the Inner Sphere. Both modern production facilities on Carlisle and Gienah operate within the Lyran Commonwealth, though the vehicle's widespread distribution ensures it appears in the arsenals of every Great House and several larger Periphery nations. The Federated Suns' March Militias prize the design particularly highly, relying on it for independent patrol and border surveillance duties where its fusion-powered endurance provides a decisive operational advantage.

The ICE variant represents the most common Succession Wars degradation of the original design. Field technicians replaced the Doorman fusion engine with a less capable internal combustion powerplant, sacrificing the rear-mounted flamer and one ton of armor to accommodate the heavier engine. Large numbers of ICE-equipped Packrats remain in service across the Inner Sphere, though early maintenance records suggest these vehicles are among the first to be scrapped in favor of restored fusion-powered replacements as new production vehicles become available.

This 2798 field modification became common among Free Worlds League planetary militias. The refit strips the rear flamer and infantry bay, replacing them with two forward-firing medium lasers. The exchange trades the vehicle's troop-carrying and concealment capabilities for increased direct-fire engagement ability, giving militia commanders a more combat-capable scout at the cost of the Packrat's original deep patrol mission profile.

Introduced in the Capellan Confederation in 2824, this variant expands the infantry bay to three tons, allowing the vehicle to carry an entire infantry platoon. The original Harvester 20K SRM-6 launcher was replaced with a lighter Hovertec twin-tube SRM-2 to make room for the expanded troop compartment, though it retained two tons of ammunition. The modification prioritizes the Packrat's transport role over its combat punch, reflecting Capellan doctrine that valued infantry insertion capability in a fast, fusion-powered platform.

text.overview: The Padilla Anti-Missile Tank represents the most technologically sophisticated member of the Padilla vehicle family, entering production in 3136 as a joint development between the Republic Armed Forces and Aldis Industries of Terra. Born from the proven effectiveness of the Advanced Point Defense System on the Aegis battle armor suit, the Anti-Missile Tank was designed to bring vehicle-scale point defense capability to combined-arms formations where it could protect an entire lance rather than a single trooper. Using the Padilla Tube Artillery Tank chassis as its foundation, the Anti-Missile Tank pairs two Advanced Point Defense mounts with an M-7 Gauss rifle for direct fire support, while stealth armor and an integrated ECM suite protect the vehicle from counter-targeting. Principes Guard armor companies adopted the type following its 3136 introduction, fielding it in fire support lances alongside conventional Padilla artillery tanks and JES III Missile Carriers.
text.capabilities:
The Padilla Anti-Missile Tank's defining systems are its pair of McArthur III Advanced Point Defense mounts, manufactured by Blankenburg and positioned to provide overlapping coverage against incoming missiles. The APDS mounts represent a vehicle-scale implementation of technology previously limited to Aegis battle armor, offering a substantially wider protective envelope than the single-mount anti-missile systems common on other vehicles. Testing confirmed that APDS-equipped vehicles in formation could significantly degrade incoming Arrow and LRM barrages, making the Anti-Missile Tank a force multiplier for any combined-arms formation facing heavy missile opposition.

Complementing the defensive systems is an M-7 Gauss rifle in a fully traversing turret, providing substantial direct fire capability against armored targets at range. The light fusion engine delivers reasonable performance for a wheeled fifty-five-ton vehicle intended to operate within a formation rather than independently. Seven and a half tons of stealth armor powered by the integrated Guardian ECM system replaces the standard armor of the base Padilla Tube chassis. While the stealth system meaningfully reduces the vehicle's sensor signature against precision-guided munitions, it does not increase physical armor protection compared to the base Tube variant, a trade-off accepted in return for improved survivability against advanced targeting systems. The light fusion engine provides the power margin needed to run both the stealth armor and APDS mounts simultaneously without taxing the power plant.
text.deployment: Assigned exclusively to Principes Guard armor formations following production approval in 3136. Standard deployment doctrine pairs Anti-Missile Tanks in fire support lances alongside two conventional Padilla Tube Artillery Tanks and a JES III Missile Carrier, creating a formation where point defense coverage protects the artillery vehicles from missile saturation while the Gauss rifle addresses armored threats at direct fire range. The stealth armor and integrated ECM suite favor deployment in forward positions where the vehicle's reduced sensor signature provides additional survivability against precision-guided munitions targeting systems.
text.battleHistory:
The Padilla Anti-Missile Tank's development history begins with the Aegis battle armor and the Advanced Point Defense System that distinguished it from competing Republic designs. Following the APDS's proven combat effectiveness on the Aegis suit in Republic service, RAF High Command initiated a program through RISC to develop a vehicle-scale implementation that could extend point defense capability to the formation level. The program benefited substantially from detailed performance data collected from APDS-equipped Aegis suits in field operations, accelerating development of the vehicle-scale system beyond what laboratory work alone could have achieved.

Aldis Industries on Terra received the production contract, building on its existing experience with the Padilla Tube Artillery Tank chassis. Initial development focused on replacing the tube artillery system with the McArthur III APDS mounts, a conceptually straightforward conversion. The more consequential design decision came when a member of the Aldis engineering team noted that the Betelgeuse design bureau had successfully integrated stealth armor and ECM into the Regulator II heavy tank. Aldis engineers adopted the same approach, replacing the standard Padilla armor with stealth material and adding the Guardian ECM suite to power it. The change shifted the vehicle's survivability philosophy from raw armor protection to sensor evasion and formation defense. The original tube artillery piece was replaced with an M-7 Gauss rifle to provide meaningful direct fire capability alongside the point defense role.

Field testing began in 3134, with the vehicle operating in false flag evaluations concealing its advanced systems from observers. Performance proved sufficient for RAF approval of full production in 3136. Principes Guard armor companies that received first deliveries incorporated the Anti-Missile Tank into fire support lances alongside conventional Padilla Tube Artillery Tanks and JES III Missile Carriers, a formation doctrine leveraging point defense coverage to protect the more vulnerable artillery vehicles from missile saturation while the Gauss rifle engaged armored threats at direct fire range.

text.deployment: Assigned throughout the SLDF to combined-arms artillery formations alongside Chaparral Missile Artillery Tanks and TAG-equipped BattleMechs. Almost entirely destroyed during Operation Liberation and the subsequent Succession Wars, with survivors eventually passing through Com Guard possession into Republic service following the Jihad. New production resumed at the mothballed Leopard Armor facility on Terra under Word of Blake auspices in 3058 and continued under Republican ownership post-Jihad. Found primarily in Republican garrison and second-line formations in the Dark Age, with occasional pre-war examples appearing in mercenary inventories at prices far exceeding their practical value.

A Succession Wars modification performed exclusively by House Liao on Padilla hulls stripped of their Arrow IV launchers and target acquisition gear during the resource crises of the early Succession Wars. FarFire LSR-Launcher XXs were installed in place of the original system, allowing the hulls to remain nominally in service as fire support vehicles despite the loss of their Arrow IV precision capability. No documentation exists of this modification being performed by any faction other than the Capellan Confederation, and the conversion is considered rare even within former Liao inventories.

Republic of the Sphere primary tube artillery vehicle from 3077 forward, serving across Principes Guard and Standing Guard formations as the standard artillery support platform. The wheeled configuration is favored in garrison and second-line roles where road mobility is more operationally relevant than cross-country agility. Broader logistical support from standard Inner Sphere artillery munitions makes the base Tube variant the most commonly supplied and easiest to maintain across the Republic's diverse military districts.

The (AMS) field refit converts the tube artillery system to a McArthur III Advanced Point Defense System, creating a dedicated anti-missile escort vehicle suited to accompanying high-value convoys or artillery formations under persistent missile threat. Found in specialized Republic formations where the operational threat from missile-heavy opponents justifies a dedicated point defense asset. Shares tactical doctrine with the Padilla Anti-Missile Tank and can operate alongside it in formations that require overlapping coverage.

The (LTC) variant equips a Light TC artillery piece favored in formations where extended indirect fire range is prioritized over higher rate of fire. Found in Republic artillery battalions tasked with interdiction and counter-battery missions at ranges beyond the Thumper system's effective envelope. The Light TC's longer reach makes the (LTC) a common assignment for units responsible for suppressing enemy artillery before forward forces close to direct engagement.

The most widely produced and deployed Tube Artillery variant, the (Thumper) configuration benefits from the Thumper artillery system's extensive logistical support across Inner Sphere militaries. Standard issue in Republic artillery formations and increasingly common in successor state militaries that acquired the type through trade or licensing from Republic sources. The Thumper's broad ammunition availability across the Inner Sphere makes this variant the preferred configuration for units operating in theaters where supply chain continuity cannot be guaranteed.

text.overview: The Paladin Defense System is a super-heavy tracked combat vehicle built from Capellan Confederation designs captured by the Federated Suns during the Victoria War of 3105. Kallon Weapon Industries put the vehicle into production in 3109, establishing it as a dedicated long-range artillery platform for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. At 130 tons, the Paladin is one of the heaviest conventional combat vehicles fielded by any Inner Sphere power. It was designed to deliver sustained indirect fire support from well behind the front lines, coordinating with forward spotters to blanket distant targets with artillery fire. The design found its primary role with planetary militias and dedicated artillery battalions rather than fast-moving frontline regimental combat teams, where its massive bulk and slow speed would have been a liability.
text.capabilities:
The Paladin's primary armament consists of twin turret-mounted Kallon Weapon Industries Vicar Long Tom artillery pieces, giving it devastating indirect firepower at extreme range. The vehicle carries sixty rounds of ammunition in a hull-mounted bay protected by CASE, though this supply is widely considered insufficient for sustained operations. Most Paladin batteries compensate by towing dedicated ammunition trailers using the vehicle's integrated trailer hitch. One ton of dedicated communication equipment allows crews to maintain constant contact with forward spotters and coordinate fire missions across extended distances.

The Nissan 260 XL fusion engine propels the 130-ton vehicle to a modest 32 kilometers per hour, making it one of the slowest combat vehicles in active service. This limitation is accepted as a necessary trade-off for the sheer weight of fire the Paladin brings to the battlefield. Protection comes from eleven and a half tons of Durallex Special Heavy ferro-fibrous armor with CASE, providing adequate defense for a vehicle intended to operate well behind friendly lines. For self-defense, the Paladin mounts a pair of Diverse Optics extended range medium lasers and two Mydron miniguns in forward-facing positions. These weapons offer limited protection against infantry and light vehicles that close to contact range, but the Paladin remains heavily dependent on screening forces for close-in defense.
text.deployment: The majority of Federated Suns Paladins serve with planetary militias and dedicated artillery battalions. The vehicle is too slow and cumbersome for the fast-moving frontline light combat teams that form the core of Davion offensive doctrine. Once produced exclusively for the Federated Suns at Kallon facilities on Kirklin and Victoria, the design's proliferation accelerated during the Capellan and Draconis Combine invasions of the mid-3140s. Captured vehicles entered service with both aggressor states, giving the Confederation ironic access to its own stolen design for the first time since the Victoria War. Republic of the Sphere forces also fielded the Paladin in limited numbers before the fall of Fortress Republic.
text.battleHistory:
The Paladin Defense System originated as a Capellan Confederation design, its plans captured by the Federated Suns during the Victoria War of 3105. When Davion forces seized Victoria, they acquired the production blueprints along with the planet's industrial infrastructure. The Capellan Confederation had developed the vehicle as a strategic fire support platform, and the Federated Suns' military leadership, well aware of the cost their forces had paid fighting against it, wasted no time putting the design into production. The Strategios directed Kallon Weapon Industries to begin manufacturing the Paladin at facilities on both Kirklin and the newly captured Victoria, with full-scale production beginning by 3109.

The Paladin found its niche within the AFFS as a garrison and defensive asset rather than an offensive weapon. Frontline commanders nonetheless pressed the vehicle into service whenever it was available, sometimes with poor results. During the Draconis Reach campaign, a company of Paladins reinforced the pro-Davion defenders of Harrow's Sun. The local commander, captivated by the prospect of twenty-four Long Tom tubes under her command, attached the company to an armored battalion and ordered it forward. Fast-moving Dragoon striker companies overran and captured the Paladins before they could fire a shot. The twelve captured vehicles became the foundation of a new planetary militia force loyal to the Dragon.

The Capellan invasion of the Federated Suns brought the Paladin into heavy defensive fighting around the worlds near Tikonov. On Alrescha, a pro-Davion militia held a firebase for three weeks against a combined-arms battalion of Liao Chargers. The Paladins' sustained day-and-night bombardments prevented the attackers from halting or establishing forward bivouacs. By the time the defenders withdrew, each vehicle had emptied twelve ammunition trailers, and the firebase grounds were covered in the ash-like residue of cannon propellant.

The Republic Remnant on Galatea also put Paladins to effective use. Fighting against the Jade Falcons, Redleg Company discarded conventional artillery doctrine and fought a mobile campaign, using screening units and RAF BattleMech support to fire and displace repeatedly. The psychological impact of shells raining from all directions proved as damaging as the physical effects, and four Paladins were isolated and destroyed during the fighting. Their crews were recognized by Damien Redburn for providing sterling and necessary service under extreme conditions.

text.overview: The Palmoni Assault Infantry Fighting Vehicle was an 85-ton tracked combat vehicle designed by Aldis Industries on Terra for the Word of Blake's Protectorate Militia forces. Introduced in 3076, the Palmoni was conceived as a heavy infantry transport capable of delivering large formations of conventional infantry directly into contested zones under fire. Aldis Industries, long renowned for producing dependable if unimaginative armored vehicles, built the Palmoni to Word of Blake military specifications. The vehicle's generous eight-ton infantry bay and mixed weapons loadout gave Protectorate garrisons a single platform that could transport troops and provide meaningful fire support. Though overshadowed by its later Republic-era successor, the Palmoni served as the foundation for an entire family of assault transports.
text.capabilities:
The Palmoni shares its basic hull and drivetrain with the later Trajan, built around a fusion engine that pushes the 85-ton vehicle to a modest flank speed of just over fifty kilometers per hour. Its primary armament consists of twin multi-missile launchers mounted in the turret, giving crews the flexibility to load long-range or short-range munitions depending on the tactical situation. A light autocannon and an extended-range medium laser round out the turret weapons, providing credible direct-fire support at medium range. Four light machine guns cover all facings, offering some deterrent against unarmored infantry attempting to close with the vehicle. A pair of anti-missile systems mounted forward help protect against incoming missile fire.

The Palmoni's distinguishing feature from its Republic successor is its Improved C3 computer, which allowed it to network with other Word of Blake units using the same system. Thirteen and a half tons of standard armor provide reasonable protection, though the vehicle's slow speed and middling armor coverage make it vulnerable in prolonged engagements against dedicated assault units. The design trades offensive punch for transport capacity, relying on its carried infantry to provide the decisive combat power once delivered to the objective.
text.deployment: The Palmoni was deployed exclusively with Word of Blake Protectorate Militia units during the final years of the Jihad. Its Improved C3 computer integrated the vehicle into Blakist command networks, allowing militia formations to share targeting data across their defensive positions. The vehicle was found on nearly every planet liberated by the Coalition in late 3077 and 3078, proof of the scale of Aldis's production effort for the Word.
text.battleHistory:
Aldis Industries developed the Palmoni during the Jihad to meet the Word of Blake's need for a robust infantry transport vehicle. The Protectorate Militia forces defending conquered worlds required a vehicle that could move their large conventional infantry formations into position while providing covering fire. Aldis, best known for the Behemoth Assault Tank, the Demolisher, and a range of weapons carriers, was an unexpected choice for the contract. The Capellan branch of Aldis had produced the Zhukov, but the Palmoni represented their first entirely new combat vehicle design in decades.

The Palmoni first saw combat on Wasat in 3077, where it caught Coalition forces off guard. Duchess Rousset-Marik's troops, expecting a conventional heavy tank, were unprepared for the infantry that poured from the vehicle's bay. Combined fire from the Palmoni's missile launchers and its dismounted troops devastated elements of the local Home Guard in under two minutes. Despite this effectiveness, Coalition forces found little use for the Palmoni after liberating Protectorate worlds. The vehicles were seen as tools of the Blakist occupation and carried an unwanted association with the Word. Most were left in the hands of newly established planetary militias, where they served adequately but without enthusiasm. The Palmoni's basic design proved sound enough that Aldis would later rework it into the Trajan for Republic service.

text.deployment: Introduced in 3135, this upgrade fits vehicular jump jets to the Pandion chassis, granting a degree of terrain-clearing maneuverability that partially addresses the standard model's limitations over broken ground. The jump capability allows the vehicle to clear obstacles and reposition rapidly during engagements, making it significantly more versatile in urban and wooded environments where traditional WiGE craft struggle.

The 3140 upgrade trades some of the Pandion's characteristic speed for heavier hitting power. Medium re-engineered lasers replace the original energy weapons, giving crews the ability to defeat heavier armor targets that the standard model's armament would struggle against. Laser insulators fitted to each weapon help manage the increased heat output of the new armament, preserving crew comfort during sustained engagements.

Mass produced and sold at a discount in bulk, the standard Partisan AA Vehicle has seen widespread use since its introduction. The largest purchaser has been the Magistracy of Canopus, followed closely by the FWLM and the Duchy of Andurien. The expansion of Canopian aerospace forces has forced the FWLM to strengthen its defensive anti-aircraft forces in both frontline and militia formations.

In 3134, Kallon offered an upgraded Partisan AA Vehicle with longer-ranged hypervelocity autocannons and a targeting computer. The tank's close-in defenses were also improved with the addition of a rocket launcher. This variant has seen increasing adoption among commands seeking improved standoff engagement capability.

Deployed across the former Federated Commonwealth and its successor states, standard Air Defense Tanks anchor combined-arms anti-aircraft formations. Their effectiveness increases dramatically when deployed in networked groups, making them a priority asset for garrison commands defending critical installations.

Developed when Nanking was under Word of Blake occupation, the fuel cell variant was initially produced at Loyalty. It mounts paired LB 10-X autocannons, twin AC/2s, machine guns, and an anti-missile system alongside its C3 slave, offering a cost-effective alternative to the fusion-powered standard.

The company command variant carries dual C3 master units, enabling coordination of an entire company-level C3 network. The removal of the light autocannons to accommodate the systems is offset by the comprehensive targeting data distribution across the formation.

Mounting a single C3 master unit in place of the standard slave, the lance command variant anchors four-vehicle air defense lances. The twin Ultra AC/5s replacing the LB 10-X autocannons trade engagement flexibility for a sustained rate of fire effective against fast-moving targets.

Also developed during the Jihad at Loyalty, the LRM variant carries four Artemis IV-guided LRM-15 launchers for precision indirect fire support. Like the Cell variant, it uses a fuel cell engine and was later also produced at the recovered Nanking facility.

An extreme expression of the rotary autocannon concept, the Quad RAC variant mounts four Rotary AC/2s slaved to a targeting computer and C3 network. An XL engine provides necessary weight savings, and armor protection is increased nearly forty-five percent over the standard XL variant.

Entering service in 3067, the rotary autocannon variant mounts paired Rotary AC/5s and LB 2-X autocannons. The sheer volume of fire this variant produces makes it devastating against conventional fighters and VTOLs, though ammunition consumption limits sustained operations.

The XL variant uses a GM 240 XL engine to free weight for twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armor, twin LB 10-X autocannons, and twin Ultra AC/2s. Its substantially higher cost has limited adoption to elite units and well-funded garrison commands willing to accept the XL engine's vulnerability.

Concentrated in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League where Kallon's primary factories operate, the standard Partisan serves with garrison and militia commands across the Inner Sphere. The Outworlds Alliance is a notable exception, where air superiority concerns are addressed through other means. Sales to the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine have fluctuated with diplomatic relations over the centuries.

The AC/2 variant sees limited deployment, with most examples serving in militia formations that received them as surplus. The lighter weapons offer greater range but significantly reduced hitting power, making this variant less popular than the standard model among units that can choose their equipment.

Militia units across the former Federated Commonwealth adopted the C3 field refit as an affordable force multiplier. The CASE protection and C3 slave unit allowed older Partisans to contribute meaningfully to networked combined-arms formations without the expense of a full upgrade to the Air Defense Tank standard.

Produced exclusively at Kirklin, the fuel cell variant represents Kallon's modernization of the Heavy Tank platform for post-Jihad service. The combination of Ultra autocannons, heavy ferro-fibrous protection, and CASE makes this variant considerably more survivable than its predecessors. Buyers have included commands across the Federated Suns and beyond.

The extended-range LRM variant addresses the enduring demand for long-range indirect fire from the Partisan platform. Four ELRM-10 launchers provide standoff capability well beyond that of any previous Partisan variant, making it a valued asset for commands defending large installations or open terrain.

The newest variant in the Partisan Heavy Tank line, the Light Gauss model trades ballistic volume of fire for precision strikes at extreme range. Four light Gauss rifles give the vehicle a distinctive engagement profile, capable of threatening aircraft and ground targets alike from distances that earlier Partisans could never reach.

The LRM variant found its niche with commands requiring indirect fire support from their air defense vehicles. Garrisons tasked with defending fixed positions appreciated the ability to engage targets beyond visual range, though the loss of dedicated anti-aircraft capability was a meaningful trade-off.

The Clan Invasion-era refit emerged as a popular modification among frontline units seeking improved anti-armor capability. Mounting twin LB 10-X autocannons and a single Ultra AC/5, this variant retained the original engine and armor while offering significantly enhanced versatility through cluster and slug ammunition options.

The standard Patton serves as the backbone of Lyran Commonwealth and Federated Suns heavy armored formations, produced simultaneously at Hesperus II and Salem through the Clan Invasion era. Lyran units received priority in initial deliveries, but the Patton spread quickly through Federated Commonwealth formations following the Steiner-Davion alliance. It remains a common sight in heavy cavalry and armored assault regiments, though production at both facilities wound down in favor of more advanced variants by the Civil War period.

The Patton-SB is a one-of-a-kind experimental prototype developed by Taurus Territorial Industries' Advanced Projects team beginning in 3079, designed specifically for vacuum and low-gravity combat. It incorporates environmental sealing, a supercharger enabling speed bursts in reduced-gravity conditions, and a Silver Bullet Gauss rifle for precision engagement. As a single prototype it has never entered mass production; TTI faces sourcing challenges for its unusual weapon systems. The design remains a proof-of-concept for potential hostile-environment vehicle programs within the Taurian military establishment.

The Taurian variant reflects decades of independent Concordat development toward hostile-environment operations. Produced by Taurus Territorial Industries on Taurus from the Dark Age era, it incorporates an LB-X autocannon and supercharger giving it performance advantages in reduced-gravity environments. Distribution within the Taurian Defense Force prioritizes units stationed in asteroid-belt and low-gravity operational areas.
text.battleHistory:
The Patton's development in the late Succession Wars represented a turning point in Lyran military technology. For decades, the Lyran Commonwealth had relied on aging and increasingly degraded designs from the Star League era. The Patton and Rommel program changed that, requiring Defiance Industries and General Motors to build entirely new engine manufacturing facilities, an unprecedented investment for a combat vehicle at the time. Security surrounding the project was extraordinarily tight, limiting even ComStar's ROM to fragmentary intelligence on the program's true specifications.

The first prototypes went to Hansen's Roughriders for field testing, chosen for their reputation for aggressive and innovative armor use. Their evaluation produced a massive follow-on contract, and once in full production the Patton and its companion Rommel quickly became standard in both Lyran heavy armored regiments and AFFS formations. The tanks' effectiveness overcame persistent complaints about the expense of fusion powerplants in ground vehicles.

Over the following century the Patton accumulated a combat record across dozens of major engagements. Fighting on New Hessen saw Pattons prove their resilience when Davion armor engaged closing Capellan forces at short range to protect friendly formations. During Operation Hammerfall in 3137, LCAF Pattons performed throughout the Lyran offensive against former Free Worlds League worlds. Federated Suns versions saw action during the subsequent fighting for Palmyra, and documents recovered there revealed that vehicles issued to armored regiments in 3141 remained fully combat-capable years later, reflection of the robustness of the design. The Taurian Concordat developed its own independent research program toward specialized variants suited for hostile and vacuum environments, eventually producing distinct production models unique to that state.

text.deployment: The Patton Ultra is the direct predecessor to the XL model, retaining a standard fusion engine while incorporating improved secondary weapons and targeting systems. Produced at both Hesperus II and Salem from the Civil War era, it represented a cost-effective upgrade for units unable to afford the more advanced XL. The Ultra saw service through the Jihad at Salem, though the Hesperus line shifted resources toward the XL configuration earlier.
