text.deployment: The standard Pegasus serves as a light reconnaissance vehicle in virtually every major military force across the Inner Sphere. Operating in pairs or small lances, Pegasus crews scout ahead of advancing formations, relay targeting data, and identify enemy positions before committing heavier assets. The vehicle performs best when kept clear of direct engagements, using its speed to disengage when detected. Its armament is sufficient to handle most light vehicles and infantry encountered during scouting operations, though commanders consistently caution against committing Pegasi to sustained combat roles.

production.targeting: Scarborough Tracky 3 with Beagle Active Probe and TAG

text.deployment: Scarborough Manufacturers' substantially upgraded version replaces the internal combustion engine with a fusion powerplant and upgrades to ferro-fibrous armor, significantly enhancing survivability. The medium pulse laser improves accuracy in close engagements, while the Guardian ECM suite and Beagle Active Probe combination make the vehicle a considerably more capable electronic warfare platform than the original. A TAG system allows the crew to designate targets for artillery or aerospace support. Found across Draconis Combine, Free Worlds League, Federated Suns, and Capellan Confederation forces, this variant quickly became the new baseline for well-equipped Pegasus operations following its introduction.

The Missile variant trades the front-mounted medium laser for an additional SRM 6 rack, increasing short-range firepower at the cost of the backup ranged weapon. Operators who favor this configuration tend to work in dense terrain where the medium laser offers little advantage, preferring heavier missile saturation for close-in engagements. The modification is straightforward to perform in the field, and examples of the Missile variant appear in virtually every force that regularly uses the standard Pegasus.

production.manufacturer: Exeter Organization|Hellespont Industries|Quikscell Company|Scarborough Manufacturers|Valiant Systems

text.deployment: The latest Pegasus production variant combines performance advances from the X-Pulse line with the wider multi-manufacturer accessibility of earlier models. Based on the Jihad-era Sealed configuration, the MML variant drops the environmental sealing but retains the heavy ferro-fibrous armor and adds a supercharger for enhanced speed. Doubled MML launchers provide flexibility across all engagement ranges, while a Beagle probe handles electronics duties. Produced at five facilities including Hellespont on Sian, Exeter on Keystone, Scarborough on Al Na'ir, Valiant Systems on Johnsondale, and Quikscell on Broken Wheel, this is the most widely distributed advanced Pegasus configuration.

A Scarborough-developed variant from the Combine-Dominion War era, the MRM modification replaces the pulse laser and short-range missile racks with a heavier MRM system for a longer engagement envelope. The vehicle trades close-range missile saturation for the ability to engage targets at medium range without committing to close quarters. After its introduction, the MRM variant spread beyond the Draconis Combine to Republic of the Sphere forces and has maintained steady production into the Dark Age period.

Developed in the post-Jihad period, the Sealed variant features a fully sealed hull rated for operations in hazardous environments including vacuum, chemical contamination, and radiation hazards. A light fusion engine and heavy ferro-fibrous armor are paired with dual MML 3 launchers, providing a weapons suite capable of engaging targets at any range. Produced by Scarborough, Exeter, and Hellespont facilities, the Sealed variant serves in environments where standard vehicles cannot safely operate, from orbital drop scenarios to contaminated battlefields on contested worlds.

One of the earliest field modifications to the base Pegasus, the Sensors variant strips most of the vehicle's combat armament in favor of enhanced detection packages. Commands that need dedicated long-range reconnaissance platforms rather than light fire support deploy this configuration, accepting reduced offensive capability in exchange for superior intelligence gathering. The variant appears across virtually all eras and factions wherever the base Pegasus is available, reflecting the persistent demand for scout platforms that prioritize detection over firepower.

The most extreme reconnaissance configuration of the Pegasus removes all offensive weapons to maximize weight available for advanced sensors and crew equipment. Commands using this variant accept that any detected vehicle must rely entirely on speed to escape, prioritizing information gathering above all other considerations. Deployed primarily for deep-penetration missions where avoiding detection is more critical than self-defense, the Unarmed variant has seen service across virtually all factions and eras that field the base Pegasus.

An experimental prototype rather than a production vehicle, the X variant served as the engineering testbed for technologies later refined into the production X-Pulse line. Produced in only two confirmed examples at the Scarborough Manufacturing Annex on Algedi, the program was paused following a catastrophic supercharger failure during testing. The experimental equipment developed for this project informed the subsequent X-Pulse production design. This variant does not appear in organized production records and is noted here for reference only.

production.communications: Scarborough Talky 4 with C² Slave System

text.deployment: The X-Pulse variant stands as a significant performance leap over all earlier Pegasus configurations, replacing the standard missile-heavy armament with a pair of medium X-Pulse lasers and a Streak SRM 6 launcher. A powerful XL fusion engine drives the vehicle to over 180 kph, with a supercharger pushing top speed past 237 kph in short bursts, though field testing demonstrated extreme risk of catastrophic mechanical failure when the supercharger engages. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides substantially better protection than earlier variants. Built exclusively at Scarborough's Algedi facility, the X-Pulse is found primarily with Draconis Combine commands on and around the Azami worlds.

The Peregrine served in limited numbers across Houses Kurita, Liao, and Marik during the Late Succession Wars, produced from Blackwell Corporation facilities on both New Valencia and Outreach. Operators rarely committed the type to contested front-line airspace, instead assigning Peregrines to reserve formations, local militia garrisons, and civilian paramilitary units. The vehicle's speed made it acceptable for low-threat courier and patrol duties, but most commanders avoided it in any environment where it might face determined opposition. By the Clan Invasion era, most examples remaining in active service were concentrated in rear-echelon and support billets.
text.battleHistory:
Blackwell Corporation introduced the Peregrine in 3021 from their New Valencia production facility, building the type initially to meet requirements identified by Wolf's Dragoons for a dedicated close air support platform capable of operating alongside assault transports. The design entered the open market almost immediately, finding buyers across Houses Kurita, Liao, and Marik, though the Dragoons themselves declined to integrate it into their standard order of battle.

After 3030, Blackwell relocated production to Outreach, consolidating manufacturing at the Dragoons' mercenary enclave and continuing to supply the broader market. New Valencia remained active into the 3040s, with both lines operating in parallel through the early Renaissance period before the New Valencia facility wound down. By 3028, whatever prestige the Peregrine had borrowed from its Wolf's Dragoons association had eroded entirely in combat, and house militaries moved their stocks steadily toward reserve depots and local police forces. The Kurita Civilian Guidance Corps absorbed a significant number of the type, deploying them in support roles that suited the vehicle's limited practical combat value.

Peregrines serving with Kurita second-line units during the Clan Invasion fared no better against Clan opponents than they had against Inner Sphere forces. The FedCom Civil War prompted Houses Davion and Steiner to press stockpiled Peregrines back into service as stop-gap reinforcements for depleted armies, though commanders consistently confined them to rear-area and gap-filler roles well behind the front. Production at Outreach came to an end during the Jihad, when Word of Blake forces seized the world. The chronic unreliability, high maintenance burden, and genuine lethality the design posed to its own crews ultimately produced the resigned humor captured in the saying "gone watching Perries," a lasting evidence of the type's consistent absence from serious fighting throughout its operational career.

text.deployment: The Cargo variant, introduced in 3036, removes the Peregrine's weapons suite entirely in favor of expanded cargo capacity, converting the airframe into a utility transport. Widely adopted across multiple factions by logistics formations, civilian organizations, and local defense forces, this variant represents the most practical use of the airframe's genuine advantages: speed and reasonable payload. Field-converted from standard Peregrines deemed surplus to combat requirements or too expensive to sustain in an armed role, Cargo variants appeared wherever operators needed an affordable light transport helicopter and had a supply of worn-out Peregrines on hand.

text.deployment: The Kurita variant was introduced in 3033 and adopted primarily by the Kurita Civilian Guidance Corps and Combine second-line garrison forces. Modified to align with Combine operational logistics and equipment standards, this field-converted variant retained the standard airframe's fundamental strengths and shortcomings in equal measure. Like the base design, it was confined mainly to rear-area support, local defense, and paramilitary patrol roles, rarely appearing alongside front-line Combine combat units. The field refit nature of the conversion meant individual examples varied in their precise equipment fit.

text.deployment: Earthwerks markets the production Phalanx to any interested buyer regardless of affiliation, reflecting a deliberate departure from the restricted sales that characterized its prototype phase. Infantry brigades across the Inner Sphere are the most common operators, typically attaching a platoon of Phalanxes to formations that can provide close-in protection while the tank supplies fire support from standoff range. Armor units rarely acquire the design, as its limited speed and single-purpose armament offer little to combined-arms formations built around direct-fire tanks. In Lyran space, the Phalanx pairs frequently with Rottweiler battle armor squads, a combination that compensates for the tank's vulnerability to dismounted infantry while providing the armored infantry reliable heavy fire support for breaching and assault operations.

The Phalanx prototype saw extremely limited operational service following Earthwerks' decision to shelve production. Of the twelve units built, four were donated to the Free Worlds League Military, where they served in garrison and second-line roles rather than front-line combat assignments. The remaining vehicles stayed at Earthwerks' facilities on Calloway VI as engineering testbeds. At least one prototype operated in a Blakist garrison on Ohrensen during the Jihad, producing the combat footage that ultimately prompted development of the production variant. The prototype configuration, with its infantry bay and experimental amphibious systems, was never widely distributed and saw no sustained operational career beyond this limited pre-production service.

production.manufacturer: Canopus Industries Alpha|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: The standard Pike serves as the foundation of Magistracy of Canopus fire support formations, providing long-range autocannon coverage to mixed vehicle and infantry units throughout the Succession Wars and beyond. Canopus Industries Alpha's continuous production on Canopus IV has supplied the Magistracy Armed Forces since the vehicle's introduction, with Majesty Metals and Manufacturing later adding capacity at Dunianshire and Luxen. ComStar's garrison forces distributed the type widely across HPG facilities throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery, where its low operating costs made it attractive for installations requiring credible defense without significant technical infrastructure.

This field modification, appearing around 3004, replaces the three ZeusBolt AC/2s with two Autocannon/5s and seven tons of ammunition. Reducing the number of barrels by one, the modification substantially increases damage per hit, making the vehicle more effective against armored targets. The modification circulates among units able to locally source AC/5 ammunition and has been employed by a range of operators, including ComStar garrison forces and mercenary commands that acquired standard Pikes and modified them with available armaments.

production.manufacturer: Manufacturing Plant DSF-AT1|New York Vehicle Y2 Facility|York Vehicle Y2 Facility

text.deployment: Clan Diamond Shark introduced this fusion-powered version in 3055, initially produced at Manufacturing Plant DSF-AT1 on Attenbrooks before the larger New York Vehicle Y2 Facility on Trondheim became the primary Clan production site. The Clan Blood Spirit operated a parallel version from their York facility during the same period. Mounting five Ultra AC/2s in the turret with CASE-protected ammunition, the variant provides a substantially higher rate of fire than the Inner Sphere original. It supplements Clan Sea Fox vehicle Stars as a standard light fire support asset and remains available to buyers with sufficient standing to trade with the Sea Foxes.

production.targeting: Canopus Industries Alpha Magestrix Gamma Mk II

components.armor: Brooks, Inc. StarSlab/9.5 Mk II Ferro-Fibrous

text.deployment: Canopus Industries Alpha introduced this export model in 3134, designed to broaden the Pike's commercial appeal into the recovering post-Jihad market. Three Mydron Excel 5G LB 5-X Autocannons replace the ZeusBolt weapons, giving crews the option of cluster ammunition against aircraft and battle armor or solid slugs against heavier targets. A Magna 180 Fuel Cell replaces the original ICE, easing logistics for formations supported by fusion-powered vehicles. CASE bins protect the three tons of LB-X ammunition and one ton of SRM ammunition. The Marian Hegemony was among the early customers, and the variant reached distribution across the former Canopian commercial sphere.

Introduced in 2993, this field modification trades the three ZeusBolt autocannons for twin LRM-20 launchers and three tons of ammunition, significantly extending the vehicle's effective engagement range. The exchange sacrifices close-in capability entirely, leaving the crew reliant on the SRM packs at short range. The variant is best suited to open terrain engagements where screening forces keep enemies beyond minimum launch distance. It circulates as a field modification among operators who can source LRM-20 ammunition reliably, and has seen use with ComStar, Magistracy, and various mercenary formations.

Developed and marketed by Clan Sea Fox, this variant replaces all autocannons with three turret-mounted Plasma Cannons and upgrades the SRM launchers to Streak SRM-2s. A targeting computer improves accuracy against BattleMech-sized targets, and a 180 fusion engine replaces the fuel cell. CASE bins protect six tons of plasma cannon ammunition and one ton of Streak SRM ammunition. The variant is marketed specifically for anti-BattleMech roles, with plasma weaponry capable of forcing severe heat management burdens on enemy machines. Clan Sea Fox offers the type with full service and supply packages at commercial rates, targeting customers seeking an affordable counter to BattleMech forces.

Originally a Federated Suns field refit developed around 3062, the Assault Pike replaces the original ICE with a fusion engine and trades the ZeusBolt autocannons for three Rotary Autocannon/2s with four tons of ammunition. A small laser mounted on the front provides anti-infantry deterrence, and ferro-fibrous armor increases protection. The variant shifts the Pike from passive fire support to active offensive use, with the rotary autocannons capable of sustained high rates of fire against light and medium vehicles. Majesty Metals and Manufacturing formalized production at Dunianshire during the early Dark Age, making this the only Pike variant to transition from field refit to dedicated factory production outside of Canopus.

The standard Pilum fills a fire support role in combined-arms lances and companies across the Federated Suns. Its LRM-15/Artemis IV suite is most effective in open terrain at ranges exceeding 270 meters, and it is typically held at distance under escort from faster screening elements. The vehicle's flank speed allows it to reposition between fire positions quickly, a capability that experienced commanders exploit to maintain unpredictability. Urban assignments are less suitable, as the wheeled chassis limits maneuvering in rubble and the thin armor becomes a serious liability at short range. The standard configuration is found throughout the AFFS from the Clan Invasion era onward, with particular concentration in heavy armor regiments and combined-arms battalions.

The Arrow IV variant converts the Pilum from a direct fire support role into a battlefield artillery platform. The twin LRM racks are replaced with a single Arrow IV missile launcher, and two separate ammunition bays accommodate a mix of standard and specialized munitions. This configuration operates well behind the front line, relying on forward spotters or networked target data rather than direct observation. Introduced in 3059, it was fielded to units requiring organic indirect fire capability without dedicating a full artillery vehicle. The trade-off is a significant reduction in direct-fire self-defense, so this variant requires stronger close escort than the standard configuration.

The ELRM variant, introduced in 3148, extends the Pilum's engagement range through Extended LRM launchers that outreach standard missile systems. A C3 boosted slave integrates the vehicle into network-enabled lance formations, allowing it to receive and contribute targeting data across the formation. CASE protection secures the large ammunition bays against internal detonation. This variant reflects adaptation to the long-range engagement doctrines prevalent in the ilClan period, and is deployed in formations operating under combined C3 network coverage. Standalone operation is possible but sacrifices the targeting advantages the C3 link provides.

The base Pinto serves with ComStar's Com Guard and Explorer Corps. Several Com Guard divisions maintain Pinto contingents, with the 388th Division (White Banshees) and 82nd Division (Web Cutters) among the most prominent users, employing the craft in close air support and rapid-response roles. The Explorer Corps makes broad use of the design, leveraging its dual capability as gunship and light transport on expeditions where compact logistics and cargo-bay stowage are operational priorities. Its modest support footprint makes it a recurring choice for Com Guard and Explorer Corps detachments operating well beyond conventional maintenance infrastructure.

The (WoB) variant operates exclusively with Word of Blake formations during the Jihad period. After assuming control of Krupp Armament Works on Terra, Word of Blake engineers developed a modified production variant suited to Blakist operational doctrines, introducing the revised platform in 3070. The Word of Blake Fourth Division, Blake's Boldest, fields examples of this variant, and Blakist Pintos have been documented in multiple theaters during the Jihad. The design serves in direct combat support and screening roles within Blakist combined-arms formations, taking advantage of the same logistical flexibility that made the base variant valuable to its earlier ComStar operators.

text.overview: Named for a wealth-hoarding beast of Asian legend, the Pixiu Heavy Tank entered service with the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces in 3093, first seeing action during the Victoria War of the early thirty-second century. Aldis Industries developed the design at their Betelgeuse facilities as a mobile fire support platform intended to operate alongside Po II formations, but the tank rapidly demonstrated capabilities that extended well beyond that original mandate. Combining long-range firepower with stealth armor and exceptional mobility for its weight class, the Pixiu established a formidable reputation across Capellan front lines. The design's effectiveness became so widely recognized that Republic of the Sphere and Federated Suns commanders came to regard even suspected Pixiu positions as serious threats, frequently diverting artillery assets to suppress them rather than risk a direct engagement.
text.capabilities:
The Pixiu is a seventy-ton tracked vehicle built around the combination of extreme range, stealth, and speed. Its primary offensive system is the Inokuma Gauss Rifle, a powerful long-range weapon capable of engaging targets at distances that most comparable vehicles cannot match. The Sian/Ceres Serval Thunderbolt 5 missile launcher provides flexible fire support and allows the crew to engage multiple threat types without repositioning. A Ceres Fire Flower conventional flamer rounds out the armament, offering close-defense utility and the ability to start concealing fires when the crew needs to disengage.

The Pixiu's most distinctive characteristic is its Ceres Heavy Stealth armor, paired with the integrated Guardian ECM Suite carried by the Olmstead 44 communications system. Together, these systems significantly degrade enemy targeting solutions at range, compounding the already-substantial challenge of engaging a fast-moving vehicle. The Magna 350 XL fusion plant grants a top speed of 86 kph, exceptional for a vehicle of its mass.

The primary trade-off is ammunition endurance. Both the Gauss rifle and the Thunderbolt launcher carry limited rounds, and extended engagements can exhaust stores quickly. The flamer provides a last-resort option when ammunition runs low, but cannot substitute for the main battery against armored opponents. Crews must manage their shots carefully and disengage before stocks run critical.
text.deployment:
Production of the Pixiu is allocated primarily to the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, with smaller numbers released to the Magistracy of Canopus Armed Forces. The standard employment doctrine pairs one platoon of Pixius with two platoons of shorter-ranged vehicles, typically the Po II, forming a heavy armored company that can control engagement range while the supporting elements maneuver. This formation allows the Pixiu to engage at distances where its stealth armor provides maximum benefit, drawing enemy fire while complementary vehicles press forward.

Only the most prestigious and combat-proven CCAF formations receive Pixius in large numbers. Junior and garrison commands typically operate one or two machines attached to anchor a company's long-range fires, rather than fielding them as an independent element.
text.battleHistory:
The Pixiu entered production at Aldis Industries on Betelgeuse in 3093, initially conceived to complement the Po II in combined-arms formations. Early service during the Victoria War demonstrated that the design could operate effectively independent of that support role, leading to its adoption across a wider range of Capellan commands over the following decades.

One of the most documented engagements involving the Pixiu took place on Sarna in 3113, when elements of Stone's Lament were dispatched to raid the important Capellan world and pin down the Prefectorate Guard. The Capellans occupied defensive positions in fortifications outside the Tengo Aerospace factory in Backtal, making use of fixed defenses and heavy mine fields to hold the Republic attackers. While the bulk of the Lament assaulted the main lines, an armored detachment moved through the radioactive badlands north of Backtal to outflank the garrison. A company of Pixius positioned outside the dead city of Narais intercepted this force and drove off the leading Republic hovercraft with Gauss rifle fire.

The flanking column included M1 Marksman assault tanks crewed by Lament veterans, and the resulting battle tested the Pixiu company to its limits. The Capellan crews exploited the crater-pocked terrain around Narais, maneuvering in reverse gear to keep their most heavily armored facing toward the enemy and maintain optimal range. Stealth armor and disciplined gunnery blunted the Marksmens' fire advantage despite the disparity in individual crew quality. The engagement ended with the Pixiu company neutralizing two Marksmen while losing three of their own. Though the Capellans ultimately fell back from the position, their resistance consumed the flanking element's ammunition reserves and forced the Lament's commander to abort the envelopment. The Prefectorate Guard withdrew in good order, preserving the regiment.

The battle outside Narais became a frequently cited example of how the Pixiu's design philosophy, trading crew numbers and raw firepower for stealth and range, could offset qualitative disadvantages when terrain and tactics allowed the crew to dictate terms of engagement.

text.deployment: The standard Plainsman serves across Taurian Concordat combined-arms formations, most commonly in screening and fire support roles within armor-heavy Corps and brigade structures. A mainstay throughout the Concordat's standing forces, it can also be found in second-echelon units and reserve formations across the Inner Sphere and many Periphery states. Its proven reliability and modest logistics footprint make it a practical choice wherever hover-mobile fire support is needed without the premium cost of more sophisticated designs.

Pinard recommends that every standard Plainsman platoon include at least one Scout to extend the formation's situational awareness. The Beagle Active Probe allows the Scout to serve in forward reconnaissance and enemy probing roles that the base variant cannot fill. Procurement realities mean that most formations acquire the Scout at the company level rather than per platoon, typically one per company on average. Its lighter armament requires it to operate with standard Plainsmen during any contested advance.

The Streak variant entered production during the Jihad era, reinforcing Taurian formations engaged in the border conflicts that characterized the period. Holly Streak SRM-4 racks replace the standard Harvester SRM-6 launchers, trading raw missile volume for the improved hit probability of Streak guidance technology. The Holly racks were simultaneously released as a field upgrade kit, allowing existing Plainsmen to be converted by unit technicians. The reliable forward Harvester SRM-2 launcher is retained unchanged across the conversion.

production.manufacturer: Alliance Defenders Limited|Ceres Metals Industries|Ceres Metals Industries|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: The Po serves as the primary combat vehicle for Capellan garrison formations lacking sufficient 'Mech forces. Planetary militias along the Magistracy and Capellan March borders are heavily supplied with the type. Its low cost makes it a popular choice among mercenary formations across the Inner Sphere, with export sales channeling needed revenue back to the Confederation. Capellan Reserve Cavalry units use it extensively alongside the Confederation Defense Force. The design's availability through multiple production facilities across the Periphery ensures continued support even in supply-constrained theaters.

The HV Prototype saw extremely limited production, with the first six vehicles combat-tested on Menke before being declared deployment-ready. These prototypes were assigned to CCAF assault formations for operations on Hsien, where their extended-range autocannons demonstrated real potential. Significant losses during the assault, combined with cost concerns over the experimental hardened armor and fusion engine pairing, drove engineers toward the production fuel-cell variant. The prototype configuration was not carried forward into full production and appears only in very limited CCAF inventories.

The production HV variant resolved the prototype's weight and cost problems by substituting a fuel cell engine for the prototype's fusion plant. The recovered mass was applied to additional hardened armor, bringing protection to fourteen tons. This combination of high-velocity long-range firepower and exceptional protection for the weight class gives the production HV a distinct tactical identity separate from the base Po. The variant is concentrated in elite Capellan formations, particularly McCarron's Armored Cavalry, the Citizen's Honored brigade, and the defensively-oriented Victoria Commonality Rangers.

production.manufacturer: Ceres Metals Industries|Ceres Metals Industries|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: Introduced in 3069 for the CCAF's shadow lance formations, the LB-X variant found immediate acceptance among crews who valued the ability to switch between armor-penetrating standard rounds and anti-personnel cluster munitions. The type saw large-scale deployment along the Capellan March border during the Jihad. CCAF shadow lances equipped with the variant proved effective at exploiting the confusion of Jihad-era Inner Sphere operations. Majesty Metals and Manufacturing added production at Dunianshire and Luxen in the Dark Age, extending the type's availability throughout the Magistracy into the ilClan era.

production.manufacturer: Ceres Metals Industries|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: The Light Gauss variant originated as an FWLM testbed in the late 3050s, with the Free Worlds League experimenting with extended-range alternatives for their purchased Po fleets. Despite improved range over the standard autocannon, the reduction in raw firepower made the variant unpopular with tank crews and Ceres discontinued production in 3064. The design experienced a second life in the Dark Age, when Majesty Metals and Manufacturing began producing it at Dunianshire and Luxen for Magistracy customers who valued the longer engagement range in a frontier defensive role.

The Po II entered service with the St. Ives Lancers and spread rapidly to frontline CCAF formations throughout the Dark Age period. Most concentrated deployments are in contested Tikonov Corridor worlds and along the Confederation's active borders, where the dramatically increased firepower over the original Po has produced consistent tactical surprises for opponents accustomed to the lighter-armed predecessor. Production at both Menke and St. Ives supports Confederation demand, with limited export availability given the priority placed on CCAF equipping.

text.overview: The Po II Heavy Tank serves as a generational advance over its predecessor, trading the original's simplicity and low cost for a comprehensive weapons suite befitting a true main battle tank. Developed by Ceres Metals Industries following Blakist destruction of the St. Ives production facilities during the Jihad, the Po II incorporates an XL fusion engine, an Ultra Autocannon/20, and multiple missile systems into a redesigned hull derived from the familiar Po. Entering production in 3077, it became the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces' primary heavy tracked combat vehicle in the Dark Age, serving alongside surviving Po units rather than replacing them wholesale. Export demand from allied Periphery states and steady domestic requirement have kept both Menke and St. Ives lines running at capacity.
text.deployment: The Arrow IV variant replaced the main autocannon with a Luxor Mobile Battery Arrow IV artillery missile system, adapting the Po II hull for indirect fire support missions. Observed in limited testing on Menke, the variant provides indirect fire capability to combined arms formations lacking dedicated artillery assets. Production remains limited relative to the standard Po II, with the variant serving in specialized fire support roles within Capellan combined arms formations rather than as a front-line fighting vehicle.

The Stealth variant drops the Streak SRM launchers in favor of ECM equipment and stealth armor, providing a low-signature alternative suited to screening and deceptive operations. Originally conceived alongside the Gauss variant as a stop-gap before the Pixiu's arrival, the Stealth configuration demonstrated sufficient unique utility that limited production continued past its initial role. It serves primarily in reconnaissance and electronic deception assignments within CCAF combined arms formations, exploiting its stealth armor to degrade enemy targeting in contested engagements.

production.targeting: Sylix Systems GSL 'Evil Eye' series II

text.overview: The Pollux Air Defense Artillery tank emerged from the Star League's ambitious Space Defense System program, which required not only orbital infrastructure but an extensive network of ground-based sensors, batteries, and communications nodes spread across the Terran Hegemony. Recognizing that these installations would be prime targets for enemy aerospace assets, the Star League awarded Hadley, Incorporated a contract to develop a mobile anti-air platform capable of defending SDS ground components. Hadley partnered with General Motors, one of the Inner Sphere's largest combat vehicle manufacturers, to develop a tracked chassis suited to the role while its own engineers adapted an existing automated turret design for crewed operation. First Lord Jonathan Cameron backed the program publicly and pledged to deploy batteries of these tanks across every Hegemony world. Production began at the Hadley-General Motors facility on Pollux in 2710.
text.capabilities:
The Pollux ADA tank's firepower centers on a modified GAD-14 turret reconfigured for crewed vehicle operation. The turret mounts a Hegemony Arms DAT/96 Sniper tube artillery cannon adapted for flak munitions alongside a Blankenburg LB 10-X autocannon, allowing the crew to engage airborne targets across multiple range bands. The elevation modifications required for effective anti-air use involved significant reworking of both weapons, particularly the long Sniper barrel, and the resulting configuration reduced the tank's effectiveness in conventional ground-to-ground engagements. A Maxell DW medium laser provides intermediate-range point defense, while a front-mounted Starflash Plus small pulse laser covers the immediate close-in zone against strafing fighters. Six tons of ammunition storage supports sustained anti-air operations.

Because the ADA tank cannot access the SDS network's sensor feeds as stationary emplacements can, Hadley's engineers required a standalone sensor solution. After evaluating multiple options including the widely used Garrett systems, they selected the Sylix Systems GSL 'Evil Eye' series II, which provides simultaneous tracking and engagement solutions for scores of airborne and ground-based targets. The tank's General Motors 225-rated fusion engine delivers a cruising speed suitable for repositioning within a defensive network. Six tons of Grumman-5 ferro-fibrous armor provides adequate protection against weapons typical of fighters and light aerospace craft, though the tank was not designed to withstand sustained fire from heavy ground combatants.
text.deployment: The Pollux ADA tank was assigned to both Star League Defense Force Air Defense Artillery battalions and Hegemony planetary garrison ADA batteries, serving as the mobile component of the ground-based Space Defense System protection network. Standard doctrine positioned batteries of Pollux tanks around key SDS installation sites, where they operated alongside stationary emplacements to provide overlapping coverage against enemy fighters and aerospace craft. Their dual-mode weapons allowed crews to engage ground targets with indirect artillery fire during lulls in air threats, making the vehicles useful beyond their primary ADA mission. SLDF ADA doctrine called for the vehicles to reposition frequently to complicate enemy targeting of coverage zones.
text.battleHistory:
Production of the Pollux ADA tank began in 2710 at the joint Hadley, Incorporated and General Motors facility on Pollux, following years of development prompted by complaints from Hegemony worlds that lacked adequate ground-based air defense under the Space Defense System. From the outset, the SLDF managed distribution of the new vehicles carefully. Rather than fully equipping garrison ADA units as the Hegemony government expected, the Star League Defense Force quietly allocated deliveries on a 50/50 basis between existing regular SLDF ADA formations and the planetary batteries it was publicly building up. To conceal this arrangement, commanders publicized the delivery of a small number of tanks to each world, then staged prominent joint training exercises featuring garrison Polluxes operating alongside regular army units, creating the impression of larger garrison allocations than actually existed.

This distribution arrangement held for nearly a decade before unraveling in 2718, when Commanding General Fredasa was directly confronted by the governor of Ankaa. The governor, a former SLDF regular and reserve officer, recognized the pattern. Following the exposure, deliveries to planetary garrisons increased substantially for the next two decades, and the SLDF's own annual allocations were reduced to minimal levels. In the years leading up to the Periphery Uprising, General Aleksandr Kerensky quietly transferred large numbers of the ADA tanks from garrison duty into the regular army, in some cases moving entire batteries. These vehicles served extensively in Periphery operations before returning to the Inner Sphere, where the survivors eventually found themselves fighting the threat they had been designed to defeat during the Amaris Civil War.

Production on Pollux continued through the early Succession Wars as the planet's political status shifted from Terran Hegemony control to independence and eventually Free Worlds League jurisdiction, but output had ceased well before Pollux was absorbed into the FWL. No Inner Sphere producer revived the design, and the Pollux ADA tank gradually disappeared from active inventories through combat loss and parts exhaustion.

text.overview: The Praetorian Mobile Strategic Command HQ is a heavy tracked command vehicle developed during the early years of the Republic of the Sphere. Designed to serve as the nexus of a regiment's communication network, the Praetorian coordinates large combined-arms formations by working in tandem with smaller Tribune mobile headquarters vehicles. Each Republic battalion fielded a lance of one Praetorian and three Tribunes, creating a layered command structure that blankets a battlefield with sensor coverage and communications relay points. Produced jointly by Cyclops Incorporated on Skye and Michaelson Heavy Industries on Ruchbah and Terra, the Praetorian became one of the most recognizable Republic vehicles during its first decade of service.
text.capabilities:
The Praetorian's core asset is its ten tons of communications equipment, the heaviest suite fitted to any Republic vehicle and double the capacity of the Tribune. This system enables satellite connectivity, remote sensor relay integration, and multi-band communication channels that give coordinated forces a significant initiative advantage. A Cyclops I/3 Extended communications system and Evil Eye Block V targeting tracking suite provide the electronic backbone of the command network.

An armored motive system protects the tracked drivetrain from battle damage, improving survivability in contested areas. Durallex Special heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides thick protection befitting the vehicle's strategic importance. The modular mount system does not require the specialized tooling of a full Omni design but still allows units to tailor their vehicles with minimal effort, at roughly half the time required by comparable vehicles. A Magna Mk VI extended-range medium laser and four Garret Tread A-Pods provide defensive capability. The Pitban 210 fusion engine limits top speed to 64 km/h, encouraging commanders to remain at a safe distance from the heaviest fighting.
text.deployment: The Praetorian serves as the strategic command node in Republic combined-arms regiments, paired with three Tribunes per battalion. Following the Republic's collapse, production continued at Cyclops Incorporated on Skye and Michaelson Heavy Industries on Ruchbah, with vehicles spreading to numerous Inner Sphere factions. The vehicle's modular design has spawned a surprising number of field variants as different operators customize their Praetorians for local conditions and doctrinal preferences.
text.battleHistory:
Elements of Devlin Stone's reformist vision embraced by the Republic's military leadership led directly to rethinking how wars would be fought. Stone and his commanders, particularly Victor Steiner-Davion, recognized that greater emphasis on combined-arms operations necessitated a significant increase in battlefield coordination capability. Prototypes of both the Praetorian and Tribune were fielded during the final stages of the Capellan fighting from 3081 through 3085, with lessons from that conflict incorporated into the final production models that officially debuted in September 3091.

The Praetorian-Tribune system's success during the Capellan Crusades generated widespread interest across the Inner Sphere. The Republic's initially restrictive export policies eventually gave way to liberal distribution after it became clear that the technology had already proliferated through battlefield salvage and reverse engineering. The number of field variants is surprisingly high for units with such a comparatively short service history, proof of the design team's modular vision. As the Republic collapsed, production continued under new management at each factory, ensuring the vehicle's continued presence on battlefields across the Inner Sphere through the ilClan era.

text.deployment: The standard production Predator is the definitive expression of the design's philosophy. The Ceres Motors 270 fuel-cell engine delivers the sprint speed necessary for rapid displacement after a kill, while the Mydron Devastator LB 20-X autocannon provides reliable anti-armor firepower capable of disabling any vehicle within effective range. Hellespont Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor concentrates protection on the frontal arc where the design's doctrine demands it. This variant has seen extensive deployment with elite CCAF combined-arms formations since its introduction, including on Victoria, Second Try, and other contested worlds throughout the Capellan Crusades and into the ilClan era. It remains the primary production variant at Ceres Metals Industries on Indicass.

The (Elite) variant, introduced in 3144 and documented in the 3150 Recognition Series, serves as a further refinement of the standard Predator for high-intensity late Dark Age and ilClan-era operations. Component upgrades draw on decades of active CCAF service feedback, with modifications optimized against the increasingly capable opponents encountered during this period. The (Elite) is issued to the Confederation's premier armored formations and remains in active frontline production on Indicass. Specific technical details of the upgrade package are not widely circulated outside CCAF planning circles.

The (Original) Predator mounts an internal combustion engine rather than the modern fuel-cell powerplant, along with a less capable autocannon and conventional steel armor. This configuration reduces both sprint speed and mission endurance compared to the modern variant, limiting effective ambush operations. The essential casemate layout and tactical doctrine are retained, and the (Original) can be effective when employed correctly, but it lacks the punch and durability of the later production model. Most surviving hulls served in CCAF combined-arms formations during the latter Succession Wars before production ceased following the Spica engagement in 2974. Remaining examples are found only in militia and reserve inventories.

The standard Prowler serves as a general-purpose transport and survey vehicle across the Inner Sphere. Most major militaries maintain small numbers for operations in exotic terrain, deploying them alongside scout and reconnaissance elements rather than in front-line roles. The fully automated version produced at Terran facilities is optimized for the Explorer Corps, carrying laboratory equipment and scientific instruments alongside its standard cargo complement. Defiance Motors supplies the Lyran state, while Pinard Protectorates Limited serves the Taurian Concordat and neighboring Periphery states. This variant defines the baseline from which all other Prowler configurations are derived, retaining the original amphibious drive and active probe suite in their intended forms.

Introduced in 3140 by Millennium Industries, this upgrade addresses reliability issues identified during extended Republic service. Updated electronics and revised systems reduce crew fatigue during long-duration survey and patrol missions, while the core amphibious drive and automation suite are retained with refinements. Production is concentrated at the Terra facility, with distribution primarily to Republic and ilClan-era forces requiring a capable all-terrain platform. The 3140 Upgrade represents the current baseline for new Prowler procurement by forces with access to Millennium Industries' production output.

The ECM variant replaces the Prowler's standard electronics suite with a Guardian ECM system, converting the vehicle from a survey platform into a mobile electronic warfare asset. The cargo bay is retained, but the Beagle Active Probe is sacrificed to accommodate the Guardian system's power requirements. Performed as a field refit rather than at a dedicated production facility, this conversion appears wherever units have access to surplus Guardian hardware. The ECM Prowler is particularly valued by guerrilla forces and second-line units requiring mobile jamming capability without the cost and maintenance burden of dedicated electronic warfare vehicles.

Developed for ComStar's Explorer Corps, the Sealed variant adds comprehensive environmental protection to the standard Prowler chassis. Full hermetic sealing and enhanced life support allow the vehicle to operate in vacuum, toxic atmospheres, and radiation-intensive environments encountered during deep-space survey missions. The cargo bay is repurposed to carry specialized laboratory and analytical equipment in place of standard infantry accommodations. Production remained concentrated at the Mitchell Vehicles facility on Terra, with ComStar and later the Explorer Corps maintaining tight quality control over these research platforms. The Sealed variant saw limited distribution outside the Explorer Corps.

Developed for internal security and law enforcement roles within the Republic of the Sphere, the Security variant adapts the Prowler chassis for urban patrol and policing operations. Introduced in 3123 and produced exclusively by Millennium Industries on Terra, it is distributed to Republic security agencies and garrison forces rather than front-line military units. The Security Prowler is a common sight in Republic population centers and along strategic transit routes. Its full amphibious capability is retained, providing utility across the diverse terrain types found throughout Republic space.

production.manufacturer: Ceres Metals Industries|Defiance Motors|General Motors|Pesht Motors|Pinard Protectorates Ltd

text.deployment: The Succession Wars variant represents the inevitable simplification of the Prowler under the industrial and technological pressures of that era. The advanced automation suite is stripped in favor of a conventional multi-crew arrangement, and the cargo bay is reconfigured as a dedicated infantry compartment, giving the vehicle more direct combat utility. The long-range missile rack receives an ammunition upgrade to provide better fire support to the infantry it carries. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery produce this variant, making it the most widely encountered Prowler configuration. Its low production cost and minimal maintenance requirements ensure continued manufacture even in resource-limited facilities.

A field modification developed during the Succession Wars, the Support variant adapts the standard Prowler chassis for rear-echelon utility roles. Armament is simplified to reduce crew workload and maintenance demands, while additional cargo capacity is freed for supplies and spare parts. Performed by unit technicians rather than dedicated conversion facilities, the Support variant shows considerable variation between individual vehicles. It fills a gap between dedicated logistics transports and combat carriers in second-line and garrison formations that lack the budget for purpose-built support vehicles.

The PAT-005 is the definitive production variant of the Puma, resolving the critical flaws of its predecessors and entering service with the SLDF in 2681. Deployed in armored assault and fire-support formations, it served with Regular Armored Command units across the Star League and saw action through the final decades of the Star League era. ComStar maintained production at Pandora 'Mech Works on Terra following the Coup, keeping the design available to the Com Guards throughout the Succession Wars. Odin Manufacturing on Orestes produced the PAT-005 for the Free Rasalhague Republic's defensive formations during the late thirty-first century. The Word of Blake also fielded large numbers of the PAT-005 as the backbone of Protectorate Militia armored elements after restarting production in 3065. The PAT-005 remains the most widely recognized and most commonly encountered variant of the Puma.

The PAT-005b, designated the Royal variant, was developed in 2751 for the SLDF's Royal Divisions and served exclusively with those elite formations. The XL power plant frees sufficient weight to accommodate an extended-range particle cannon, twin Streak missile launchers replacing the original SRM rack, Artemis IV guidance on the LRM launchers, and a pulse laser at the rear. CASE protects the ammunition storage throughout the hull. Production at Pandora 'Mech Works halted with the factory's destruction or mothballing following the Amaris Coup and was not restored during the Succession Wars. After the Jihad, the production line was brought back online at the same facility to replace the PAT-007 in Republic of the Sphere service, with the design finding a new role as a capable assault vehicle for post-Jihad forces requiring proven Star League-era technology.

The PAT-007 entered production in 3069 at Pandora 'Mech Works as the standard combat vehicle for the Word of Blake Protectorate Militia. Designed to equip militia formations rather than elite units, it exchanges the original PPC and separate missile systems for a heavy particle cannon and three multi-missile launchers capable of engaging targets at both short and long range. The heavy ferro-fibrous armor and CASE provide significantly better crew protection than the original PAT-005. Machine gun arrays and a B-Pod give the tank meaningful capability in urban environments against infantry and battle armor. The C3i computer ties PAT-007 units into Blakist Level II formations, sharing targeting data across the formation and multiplying the effectiveness of coordinated fire missions. Odin Manufacturing on Orestes also produced the PAT-007 for Free Rasalhague Republic and later Clan Ghost Bear forces during the Civil War. Post-Jihad production on Terra was discontinued due to the C3i system's incompatibility with Republic of the Sphere doctrine.

The PAT-008 is a rare command variant produced in 3069 for senior Word of Blake Protectorate officers who required both survivability and direct combat capability in the field. An extended-range particle cannon linked to a dedicated targeting computer provides highly accurate long-range fire, backed by three Artemis-guided multi-missile launchers for sustained saturation fire. Six anti-missile systems and three B-Pods ring the hull to counter missiles and battle armor threats, while a Guardian ECM suite denies electronic support to nearby enemies. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor matches the protection level of the PAT-007. Produced in limited numbers and deployed exclusively to high-value command elements, the PAT-008 was rarely found in standard line formations. Post-Jihad, the design continued in production at Pandora 'Mech Works under Republic of the Sphere oversight, serving as a capable command vehicle for forces inheriting the Blakist industrial base on Terra.

The (A) configuration trades a portion of the Prime's infantry capacity for an alternate weapons arrangement suited to engagements against heavier opposition. It remains fully compatible with the standard R10 maintenance and logistics network, simplifying combined operations between configurations. The A variant is deployed by units expecting armored resistance and requiring greater direct fire capability alongside their troop delivery mission.

The (B) configuration offers a further tactical option within the R10 family, adapting the chassis for missions requiring different capabilities than the Prime or A. Like all R10 variants, the B benefits from the shared parts and logistics chain established for the platform. It is found in combined-arms formations where commanders require operational flexibility across varied mission profiles without sacrificing the core transport capabilities of the chassis.

The (Prime) configuration fulfills the infantry transport and fire support role the R10 was designed around. Its large bay accommodates a substantial complement of conventional infantry or battle armor, and the turret weapons allow the crew to engage enemy forces before, during, and after troop deployment. The Prime is the most widely distributed R10 configuration and sees service across garrison forces and planetary militias throughout the former Free Worlds League region and neighboring states. Commanders who restrict the Prime to a dedicated transport role often underutilize the design's active fire support potential.

text.overview: The Ranger Armored Fighting Vehicle is a wheeled combat vehicle produced by Valiant Systems of Johnsondale, entering service with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns in 3076. Built on an expanded derivative of the company's Striker chassis, the Ranger trades some of that design's economy for heavier armament and substantially greater armor protection. The result is a vehicle purpose-built for close-range urban combat and infantry support, occupying a niche that the lighter Striker cannot fill. The Ranger's limited engagement range and persistent naming confusion with the Fox Armored Car have kept sales modest, but its low acquisition and maintenance costs have earned it a loyal following among mercenary commands and planetary defense forces that value affordability over battlefield versatility.
text.capabilities:
The Ranger is built on a widened three-axle derivative of the Striker hull, the added axle necessary to handle the vehicle's 45-ton combat weight. The GM 250 fusion engine drives it to a flank speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with lancemates and reposition rapidly within urban terrain.

Ten tons of Valiant Buckler standard armor provides approximately thirty percent more protection than comparable vehicles in its class. That margin is significant given the design's close-range combat doctrine, which regularly places crews within direct engagement distance of their targets.

The primary armament centers on two Johnston SlavTrack arrays, each combining a Johnston Minigun with a Johnston Light Minigun. The linked configuration delivers mixed machine gun fire out to 120 meters, effective against both conventional and battle-armored infantry. Two Exostar ER Small Lasers supplement the arrays for modest ranged capability and serve as backup when ammunition runs low.

The Ranger carries notable limitations. Its sub-120-meter effective range forces crews to close under fire before the main armament becomes useful, placing heavy demands on the driver and commander. The SlavTrack arrays are maintenance-intensive, and the absence of anti-armor capability limits the vehicle to a specialist role rather than general-purpose employment.
text.deployment: The Interdictor variant was developed in 3087 to meet growing demand for electronic warfare capability at the vehicle level. Most of the machine gun ammunition supply is removed to free mass for a Guardian ECM Suite and additional armor plate. The Interdictor sacrifices most of the VV1's anti-infantry firepower in exchange for an electronic suppression bubble that degrades enemy targeting systems, disrupts C3 networks, and interferes with guided munitions in the lance's operating area. It is typically deployed in close support of more heavily armed vehicles, where it can extend its ECM coverage across the formation without being exposed to direct engagement. The Interdictor has found particular favor with forces expecting to face opponents relying heavily on advanced electronics.
text.battleHistory:
Valiant Systems developed the Ranger as a direct extension of their Striker product line, drawing on existing chassis architecture and supplier relationships to reduce development time and cost. The design brief called for a vehicle capable of supporting AFFS infantry formations in dense urban terrain, where the Striker's armament was judged insufficient against armored infantry concentrations encountered during the later Jihad period. Adding a third axle and scaling to 45 tons gave the design team enough margin to fit the dual SlavTrack arrays and substantially heavier armor.

The Ranger entered service in 3076 and was immediately committed to post-Jihad stabilization operations. At Achernar, pairs of Rangers working alongside Morningstar Command Tanks proved effective against Protectorate Locusts and Word of Blake battle armor in the confined fighting around the BattleMech factory complex. The machine gun batteries demonstrated their value against power-armored infantry in close terrain, and the additional armor allowed crews to survive engagements that would have destroyed lighter vehicles.

Despite these early successes, broader AFFS adoption was limited by the vehicle's narrow utility. The restricted engagement range drew criticism from formation commanders accustomed to vehicles with greater battlefield flexibility, and most Rangers that survived their initial deployments were transferred from armor regiments to infantry support assignments. There they were paired with APCs and heavy infantry units, a role that suited the design far better.

Sales outside the AFFS remained modest, compounded by persistent market confusion with the Fox Armored Car's similar designation. Mercenary commands and corporations showed more consistent interest than House armies, drawn by the vehicle's low purchase price and straightforward logistics. The Republic of the Sphere became a reliable if small-volume customer, purchasing Rangers for planetary militia contracts through the Dark Age period. Valiant Systems continued refining the design through successive variants, incrementally addressing the range and maintenance criticisms that limited the base model's appeal.
